metadata.title: Blow up for the critical gKdV equation III: exotic regimes
metadata.authors: Yvan Martel, Frank Merle, Pierre Raphaël

nodes.name: $L^2$-critical generalized Korteweg--de Vries equation (gKdV)
nodes.statement: \begin{equation} {\rm (gKdV)}\quad \left\{\begin{array}{ll} u_t + (u_{xx} + u^5)_x =0, \quad & (t,x)\in [0,T)\times {\mathbb R}, \\ u(0,x)= u_0(x), & x\in {\mathbb R}. \end{array} \right. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The $L^2$-critical gKdV Cauchy problem $u_t+(u_{xx}+u^5)_x=0$ on $[0,T)\times\mathbb R$ with data $u_0$.

nodes.name: Local well-posedness of (gKdV) in $H^1$
nodes.statement: The Cauchy problem is locally well-posed in the energy space $H^1$ from Kenig, Ponce and Vega \cite{KPV,KPV2}. Given $u_0 \in H^1$, there exists a unique\footnote{in a certain sense} maximal solution $u(t)$ of \eqref{kdv} in $C([0,T), H^1)$ with either $T=+\infty$, or $T<+\infty$ and then $\lim_{t\to T} \|u_x(t)\|_{L^2} = +\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Kenig--Ponce--Vega: (gKdV) is locally well-posed in $H^1$, with a unique maximal solution that either is global or has $\|u_x\|_{L^2}$ blowing up at $T$.
conclusions: there exists a unique\footnote{in a certain sense} maximal solution $u(t)$ of \eqref{kdv} in $C([0,T), H^1)$ with either $T=+\infty$, or $T<+\infty$ and then $\lim_{t\to T} \|u_x(t)\|_{L^2} = +\infty$

nodes.name: Conservation of mass and energy for (gKdV)
nodes.statement: For $H^1$ solution, the mass and the energy are conserved by the flow: $\forall t\in [0,T)$, $$M(u(t))=\int u^2(t)= M(u_0), \ \ E(u(t))= \frac 12 \int u_x^2(t) - \frac 16 \int u^6(t)= E(u_0).$$
nodes.statement_short: Along the $H^1$ flow the mass $M(u)=\int u^2$ and the energy $E(u)=\frac12\int u_x^2-\frac16\int u^6$ are conserved.
conclusions: M(u(t))=\int u^2(t)= M(u_0)
E(u(t))= \frac 12 \int u_x^2(t) - \frac 16 \int u^6(t)= E(u_0)

nodes.name: Invariances of (gKdV)
nodes.statement: Equation \eqref{kdv} has the following invariances: if $u(t,x)$ is solution of \eqref{kdv} then $-u(t,x)$, $ u(-t,-x)$ and $$\lambda_0^{\frac12}u(\lambda_0^3 (t-t_0),\lambda_0 (x -x_0)), \ \ (\l_0,t_0,x_0)\in \RR^*_+\times \RR\times \RR$$ are also solutions of \eqref{kdv}.
nodes.statement_short: Sign flip, space-time reversal and the scaling/translation family all map solutions of (gKdV) to solutions.
conclusions: $-u(t,x)$, $ u(-t,-x)$ and $$\lambda_0^{\frac12}u(\lambda_0^3 (t-t_0),\lambda_0 (x -x_0)), \ \ (\l_0,t_0,x_0)\in \RR^*_+\times \RR\times \RR$$ are also solutions of \eqref{kdv}

nodes.name: Solitons $Q_\l$ and the ground state $Q$
nodes.statement: The family of traveling wave solutions of \eqref{kdv}, called solitons, plays a distinguished role in the analysis: $$u(t,x) = Q_{\l_0}(x-\l_0^{-2} t-x_0), \ \ (\l_0,x_0)\in\RR^*_+\times \RR,$$ with \begin{equation} Q_\l(x) = \frac{1}{\l^{\frac 12} }Q \left(\frac x\l\right) ,\quad Q(x) = \left(\frac {3}{\cosh^{2}\left( 2 x\right)}\right)^{\frac14}, \quad Q''+Q^5 =Q. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The soliton family $Q_{\l}(x)=\l^{-1/2}Q(x/\l)$ built from the explicit ground state $Q=(3/\cosh^2(2x))^{1/4}$ solving $Q''+Q^5=Q$.

nodes.name: sharp Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality
nodes.statement: It is well-known that the function $Q$ is related to the following sharp Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality (\cite{W1983}) \be \forall v\in H^1,\quad \int |v|^6 \leq \int v_x^2 \left(\frac {\int v^2}{\int Q^2}\right)^2. \ee
nodes.statement_short: Weinstein's sharp Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality, whose optimizer is the ground state $Q$.
conclusions: \int |v|^6 \leq \int v_x^2 \left(\frac {\int v^2}{\int Q^2}\right)^2

nodes.name: Global existence below the mass of $Q$
nodes.statement: Moreover, from \eqref{gn}, mass and energy conservations, for initial data in $H^1$ such that $\|u_0\|_{L^2}<\|Q\|_{L^2}$, the corresponding solution $u(t)$ of \eqref{kdv} is bounded in $H^1$ and thus globally defined in time.
nodes.statement_short: Sub-threshold mass $\|u_0\|_{L^2}<\|Q\|_{L^2}$ forces the solution to stay bounded in $H^1$, hence global.
assumptions: for initial data in $H^1$ such that $\|u_0\|_{L^2}<\|Q\|_{L^2}$
conclusions: the corresponding solution $u(t)$ of \eqref{kdv} is bounded in $H^1$ and thus globally defined in time
nodes.origin_citation: classical; consequence of Weinstein's sharp Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality

nodes.name: Near-minimal mass initial data
nodes.statement: \begin{equation} \|Q\|_{L^2}<\|u_0\|_{L^2}<\|Q\|_{L^2}+\alpha_0, \ \ \alpha_0\ll1 \end{equation}
nodes.section: 1.2 On the classification of the flow near $Q$

nodes.name: Existence of blow up in the energy space for negative energy data
nodes.statement: In particular, from a rigidity theorem around solitons (\cite{MMjmpa}), the first proof of blow up in finite or infinite time was obtained (\cite{Mjams}) for initial data \be\hbox {$u_0 \in H^1$ such that \eqref{utwosmall} and $E(u_0)<0$.} \ee
nodes.statement_short: Merle: near-minimal-mass $H^1$ data with negative energy blow up in finite or infinite time, via the Martel--Merle rigidity theorem.
conclusions: blow up in finite or infinite time
nodes.section: 1.2 On the classification of the flow near $Q$

nodes.name: Minimal mass blow up solution
nodes.statement: {\it {\rm (i) Existence.} There exists a solution $S(t)\in \mathcal C((0,+\infty),H^1)$ to \fref{kdv} with minimal mass $\|S(t)\|_{L^2}=\|Q\|_{L^2}$ such that \be\| S_x(t)\|_{L^2}\sim \frac{\|Q'\|_{L^2}}{ t}\ \ \mbox{as} \ t\downarrow 0. \ee \\ {\rm (ii) Uniqueness.} Let $u$ be an $H^1$ blow up solution to \eqref{kdv} with minimal mass $\|u(t)\|_{L^2} = \|Q\|_{L^2}$. Then $u=S$ up to the invariances of the (gKdV) equation.}
nodes.statement_short: There is a minimal-mass blow up solution $S(t)$ with rate $\|S_x(t)\|_{L^2}\sim\|Q'\|_{L^2}/t$, and it is unique up to the invariances.
assumptions: Let $u$ be an $H^1$ blow up solution to \eqref{kdv} with minimal mass $\|u(t)\|_{L^2} = \|Q\|_{L^2}$
conclusions: There exists a solution $S(t)\in \mathcal C((0,+\infty),H^1)$ to \fref{kdv} with minimal mass $\|S(t)\|_{L^2}=\|Q\|_{L^2}$
Then $u=S$ up to the invariances of the (gKdV) equation.

nodes.origin_citation: Martel, Merle & Rapha\"el II; Martel & Merle 2002 (Duke)

nodes.name: The class $\mathcal{A}$ of data with decay on the right
nodes.statement: $$ \mathcal{A}= \left\{ u_0=Q+\e_0 \hbox{ with } \|\e_0\|_{H^1}<\alpha_0 \hbox{ and } \int_{y>0} y^{10}\e_0^2< 1 \right\}, $$
nodes.statement_short: Perturbations of $Q$ that are $H^1$-small and satisfy the tenth-moment decay $\int_{y>0}y^{10}\e_0^2<1$ on the right.
nodes.section: 1.2 On the classification of the flow near $Q$

nodes.statement: $$\mathcal T_{\alpha^*}=\left\{u\in H^1\ \ \mbox{with}\ \ \inf_{\l_0>0, \, x_0\in \RR} \left\|u- Q_{\l_0}\left( .-x_0 \right) \right\|_{L^2} <\alpha^*\right\}.$$

nodes.name: Sharpness of the results in \cite{MMR1, MMR2}
nodes.statement: {\it 1. Sharpness of the results in \cite{MMR1, MMR2}}. Theorem \ref{th:1} above shows the optimality of the results in \cite{MMR1, MMR2} since it proves that some decay assumption (such as $u_0\in \mathcal A$) is required to obtain a unique stable blow up rate $1/(T-t)$. This is in contrast with the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation, for which the stable blow up rate is obtained in $H^1$, without additional decay assumption (see \cite{MRjams} and references therein).
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 1.1 shows a decay assumption is genuinely needed for the universal rate $1/(T-t)$, unlike for NLS where no extra decay is required.

nodes.name: Expected instability of the exotic solutions
nodes.statement: Note from the proof that the solutions obtained in Theorem \ref{th:1} are expected to be unstable (except may be for $\nu<1$ in \eqref{th:1:1}). Indeed, they are constructed using a topogical argument involving two possible directions of instability.
nodes.statement_short: The solutions of Theorem 1.1 are expected to be unstable (possibly except $\nu<1$), since they are built by a topological argument with two instability directions.
conclusions: the solutions obtained in Theorem \ref{th:1} are expected to be unstable (except may be for $\nu<1$ in \eqref{th:1:1})

nodes.name: Complementarity with the obstruction/Liouville results
nodes.statement: {\it 2}. It is proved in \cite{Mjams, MMannals} that initial data $u_0$ such that \eqref{classe} generate solutions that blow up in finite or infinite time. The proof is by obstruction and Liouville classification and does not provide any estimate on the blow up speed. This $H^1$ result is also sharp in the sense that from Theorem~\ref{th:1}, both finite or infinite time blow up may occur in $H^1$. All these results thus complement each other.
nodes.statement_short: The $H^1$ blow-up result obtained by obstruction gives no rate; Theorem 1.1 shows both finite and infinite time blow up really occur, so the results complement each other.

nodes.name: On the role of tails
nodes.statement: {\it 3. On the role of tails.} As one can see from the proof of Theorem \ref{th:1}, the blow up rate is directly related to the precise behavior of the initial data on the right. In particular, other type of blow up speeds can be produced by similar arguments by adjusting the tail of the initial data. A similar phenomenon was observed for global in time growing up solutions to the parabolic energy critical harmonic heat flow by Gustafson, Nakanishi and Tsai \cite{NT2}. There an explicit formula on the growth of the solution at infinity is given directly in terms of the initial data which is conceptually very similar to what we observe for (gKdV). Recall that continua of blow up rates were observed in pioneering works by Krieger, Schlag and Tataru \cite{KST}, \cite{KST2} for energy critical wave problems (see also Donninger and Krieger \cite{DK}). We also refer to Fila et al. \cite{FKWY} for a formal approach in the case of the energy critical heat equation. All these results point out that the sole critical topology is not enough to classify the flow near the ground state.
nodes.statement_short: The blow up rate is dictated by the initial tail on the right; analogous tail-driven continua appear for harmonic heat flow and energy-critical wave problems.

nodes.name: On the decay assumption
nodes.statement: {\it 4. On the decay assumption}. In \cite{MMR1} (see the definition of $\mathcal A$), the assumption $\int y^{10} \e^2<1$ is not sharp. In Theorem \ref{th:1}, the solution contains a tail of the form $x^{-\theta}$ for $x\gg 1$, where $\theta\in(1,\frac {29}{18})$.
nodes.statement_short: The $\int y^{10}\e^2<1$ assumption defining $\mathcal A$ is not sharp; the solutions of Theorem 1.1 carry a tail $x^{-\theta}$ with $\theta\in(1,29/18)$.

nodes.name: Sharp decay assumption for the stable blow up rate
nodes.statement: By now, it is not clear what is the sharp decay assumption on the initial data required to get the stable blow up rate in \cite{MMR1}.
nodes.statement_short: What is the sharp decay condition on $u_0$ that guarantees the stable blow up rate of \cite{MMR1}?

nodes.name: $L^2$ scalar product $(f,g)$
nodes.statement: For $f,g\in L^2$, we note the scalar product: $$(f,g)=\int f(x)g(x)dx.$$

nodes.name: Generator of the $L^2$ scaling symmetry $\Lambda$
nodes.statement: We introduce the generator of the $L^2$ scaling symmetry $$ \Lambda f=\frac12f+yf'. $$

nodes.name: Linearized operator $L$ close to the ground state
nodes.statement: We let the linearized operator close to the ground state be: \be Lf=-f''+f-5Q^4f. \ee
nodes.definiendum: linearized operator close to the ground state

nodes.name: Geometrical decomposition of $u$ with the tail $q_0$
nodes.statement: We then consider the solution to \fref{kdv} with initial data $Q+f_0$ and claim that it admits a decomposition of the form \be u(t,x) = \frac 1{\l^{\frac 12}(t)} \left( Q_{b(t)} + \l^{\frac 12}(t) q_0(t,x(t)) \Yz + \e \right) \left( t,\frac {x-x(t)}{\l(t)}\right) +q_0(t,x) \ee for some $$\|\e(t)\|_{H^1}\ll 1$$ and where $Y_0$ is a fixed function (see Lemma \ref{lemmainvert} for the definition of $Y_0$ and Proposition \ref{le:2} for the justification of this correction term).
nodes.statement_short: The solution splits as a modulated $Q_{b}$ profile plus the $Y_0$ correction and a small remainder $\e$, on top of the free tail $q_0$.

nodes.name: Coupled modulation equations perturbed by the tail
nodes.statement: Then, explicit computations similar to the ones in \cite{MMR1} yield to leading order (neglecting $\e$ and higher order terms in $(b,\l,x)$) the set of coupled modulation equations in the setting of the decomposition \fref{uu}: \be \quad \lsl+b=0,\quad x_s = \l,\quad \frac d{ds} \left( \frac b{\l^2} + \frac 4 {\int Q} c_0 \l^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta} \right)=0. \ee
nodes.statement_short: Leading-order modulation system: $\l_s/\l+b=0$, $x_s=\l$, and $\frac{d}{ds}(b\l^{-2}+\frac4{\int Q}c_0\l^{-3/2}x^{-\theta})=0$.

nodes.name: Unperturbed modulation system (no tail)
nodes.statement: This system is to be compared to the unperturbed one obtained in \cite{MMR1}, for $u_0\in \mathcal{A}$ (without tail): \be \frac {ds}{dt} = \frac 1 {\l^3}, \quad \lsl+b=0,\quad x_s = \l,\quad \frac d{ds} \left(\frac b{\l^2}\right) =0,\ee which leads to the universal blow up regime $$\frac b{\l^2} = \ell_0, \ \ \l(t) = \ell_0 (T-t)\ \ \mbox{for some}\ \ \ell_0>0.$$
nodes.statement_short: The tail-free system of \cite{MMR1}, whose conserved quantity $b/\l^2=\ell_0$ yields the universal rate $\l(t)=\ell_0(T-t)$.

nodes.name: Explicit solution of the perturbed modulation system
nodes.statement: \be \l(s) = s^{-\beta}, \quad x(s) = \frac 1{1-\beta} s^{1-\beta},\quad b(s) =\frac {\beta}s. \ee
nodes.statement_short: The threshold solution $\l(s)=s^{-\beta}$, $x(s)=\frac{1}{1-\beta}s^{1-\beta}$, $b(s)=\beta/s$ of the tail-driven system.

nodes.name: Conclusion of the proof of Theorem 1.1 returning to the original time variable
nodes.statement:
(iv) \emph{Conclusion of the proof returning to the original time variable.} The above strategy is implemented for all $0< eta< rac{11}{20}$. Now we show how the behavior of the parameters  ref{eq:blx} (see the precise estimates in \eqref{sharp}) in renormalized time leads to the scenarios of Theorem ef{th:1} in the original time $t$ (after possible scaling and time translation to adjust constants). \smallskip 
oindent{-- Blow up in finite time:} for $  rac 13 <  eta <  rac {11}{20}. $ From \eqref{sharpintro},  ref{eq:blx}: $$\int_{s_0}^{+\infty} {\l^3(s)} ds=T<+\infty$$ and the solution $u(t)$ blows up in finite time $T$. Moreover, $$ T-t=\int_{s(t)}^{+\infty}{\l^3(s')}{ds'} \sim  rac {s^{ -( 3  eta-1)}}{3 eta-1} , \quad \l(t) \sim \left[ (3 eta-1)(T-t)ight]^{ rac { eta}{3 eta-1}}, $$ which implies $\|u_x(t)\|_{L^2} \sim \|Q'\|_{L^2} \l^{-1} (t) \sim C (T-t)^{-
u}$ for any $
u\in ( rac {11}{13},+\infty).$ \medskip 
oindent{-- Grow up in infinite time:} for $  eta =  rac 13, $ the solution $u(t)$ is global in time since $\int_{s_0}^{+\infty} {\l^3(s)} ds =+\infty$. Moreover, for some $c_0$ and some $c_1 >0$, $$ t=\int_{s_0}^{s(t)}{\l^3(s')}{ds'} = \log s + c_0 +O(s^{- rac 1{10}}),\quad s\sim c_1 e^t ,\quad \l(t)\sim c_1^{- rac 13} e^{- rac t 3} . $$ This means grow up in infinite time for $u(t)$ with exponential growth. Scaling and time translation lead to any exponential rate $e^{-ct}$, $c>0$. Finally, for $0< eta<  rac 13,$ we also obtain a global solution $u(t)$ since $$\int_{s_0}^{+\infty} \l^3(s) ds \geq 2^{-3} \int_{s_0}^{+\infty} s^{-3  eta} ds = +\infty,$$ and $$t= \int_{s_0}^{t(s)} \l^3(s') ds' \sim  rac 1{1-3  eta} s^{1-3  eta} , \quad \l(t) \sim (1-3  eta)^{ rac  eta{1-3  eta}} t^{ rac  eta{1-3  eta}} , $$ which means grow up rates $t^
u$ at $+\infty$, for any $
u= rac { eta}{1-3 eta}>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate $dt=\l^3 ds$ with $\l(s)=s^{-\beta}$: $\beta\in(1/3,11/20)$ gives finite-time blow up at rate $(T-t)^{-\nu}$, $\beta=1/3$ exponential grow up, $\beta<1/3$ power grow up.

nodes.name: Set up the range of $\beta$ and the return to original time
nodes.statement: (iv) \emph{Conclusion of the proof returning to the original time variable.} The above strategy is implemented for all $0<\beta<\frac{11}{20}$. Now we show how the behavior of the parameters \fref{eq:blx} (see the precise estimates in \eqref{sharp}) in renormalized time leads to the scenarios of Theorem \ref{th:1} in the original time $t$ (after possible scaling and time translation to adjust constants).
nodes.statement_short: Record that the construction works for $0<\beta<11/20$ and that the parameter laws must now be read in the original time $t$.

nodes.name: Finite time blow up for $\frac13<\beta<\frac{11}{20}$
nodes.statement: {-- Blow up in finite time:} for $ \frac 13 < \beta < \frac {11}{20}. $ From \eqref{sharpintro}, \fref{eq:blx}: $$\int_{s_0}^{+\infty} {\l^3(s)} ds=T<+\infty$$ and the solution $u(t)$ blows up in finite time $T$. Moreover, $$ T-t=\int_{s(t)}^{+\infty}{\l^3(s')}{ds'} \sim \frac {s^{ -( 3 \beta-1)}}{3\beta-1} , \quad \l(t) \sim \left[ (3\beta-1)(T-t)\right]^{\frac {\beta}{3\beta-1}}, $$ which implies $\|u_x(t)\|_{L^2} \sim \|Q'\|_{L^2} \l^{-1} (t) \sim C (T-t)^{-\nu}$ for any $\nu\in (\frac {11}{13},+\infty).$
nodes.statement_short: $\int\l^3ds<\infty$ gives $T<\infty$ and $\l(t)\sim[(3\beta-1)(T-t)]^{\beta/(3\beta-1)}$, i.e. rate $(T-t)^{-\nu}$ with $\nu>11/13$.

nodes.name: Grow up in infinite time for $0<\beta\leq\frac13$
nodes.statement: {-- Grow up in infinite time:} for $ \beta = \frac 13, $ the solution $u(t)$ is global in time since $\int_{s_0}^{+\infty} {\l^3(s)} ds =+\infty$. Moreover, for some $c_0$ and some $c_1 >0$, $$ t=\int_{s_0}^{s(t)}{\l^3(s')}{ds'} = \log s + c_0 +O(s^{-\frac 1{10}}),\quad s\sim c_1 e^t ,\quad \l(t)\sim c_1^{-\frac 13} e^{-\frac t 3} . $$ This means grow up in infinite time for $u(t)$ with exponential growth. Scaling and time translation lead to any exponential rate $e^{-ct}$, $c>0$. Finally, for $0<\beta< \frac 13,$ we also obtain a global solution $u(t)$ since $$\int_{s_0}^{+\infty} \l^3(s) ds \geq 2^{-3} \int_{s_0}^{+\infty} s^{-3 \beta} ds = +\infty,$$ and $$t= \int_{s_0}^{t(s)} \l^3(s') ds' \sim \frac 1{1-3 \beta} s^{1-3 \beta} , \quad \l(t) \sim (1-3 \beta)^{\frac \beta{1-3 \beta}} t^{\frac \beta{1-3 \beta}} , $$ which means grow up rates $t^\nu$ at $+\infty$, for any $\nu=\frac {\beta}{1-3\beta}>0$.
nodes.statement_short: $\int\l^3ds=+\infty$ gives a global solution, with $\l(t)\sim c_1^{-1/3}e^{-t/3}$ when $\beta=1/3$ and $\l(t)\sim t^{\beta/(1-3\beta)}$ when $\beta<1/3$.

nodes.name: The functional space ${\mathcal Y}$
nodes.statement: Let the functional space ${\mathcal Y}$ be the set of functions $f\in \mathcal C^\infty({{\mathbb R}},{{\mathbb R}})$ such that \begin{equation} \forall k\in \mathbb{N},\ \exists C_k,\, r_k>0,\ \forall y\in {{\mathbb R}},\quad |f^{(k)}(y)|\leq C_k (1+|y|)^{r_k} {e^{-|y|}}, \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Smooth functions all of whose derivatives decay like $(1+|y|)^{r_k}e^{-|y|}$.
nodes.genus: the set of functions $f\in \mathcal C^\infty({{\mathbb R}},{{\mathbb R}})$

nodes.name: Invertibility of $L$
nodes.statement: {\rm (i)} There exists a unique $\Yz\in \mathcal Y$, even, such that \be L \Yz= 5 Q^4 ,\quad (Q,\Yz)=-\frac 34 \int Q . \ee {\rm (ii)} There exists a unique function $P$ such that $P' \in \mathcal{Y}$ and \be (L P)'={\Lambda} Q, \ \ \lim_{y \to -\infty} P(y) = \frac 12 \int Q, \ \ \lim_{y \to +\infty} P(y) =0, \ee \be (P, Q) = \frac 1{16} \left(\int Q\right)^2 > 0,\quad (P, Q')=0. \ee
nodes.statement_short: There is a unique even $Y_0\in\mathcal Y$ with $LY_0=5Q^4$ and $(Q,Y_0)=-\frac34\int Q$, and a unique $P$ with $(LP)'=\Lambda Q$, prescribed limits and $(P,Q)>0$.
conclusions: {\rm (i)} There exists a unique $\Yz\in \mathcal Y$, even, such that \be L \Yz= 5 Q^4 ,\quad (Q,\Yz)=-\frac 34 \int Q . \ee

{\rm (ii)} There exists a unique function $P$ such that $P' \in \mathcal{Y}$ and \be (L P)'={\Lambda} Q, \ \ \lim_{y \to -\infty} P(y) = \frac 12 \int Q, \ \ \lim_{y \to +\infty} P(y) =0, \ee \be (P, Q) = \frac 1{16} \left(\int Q\right)^2 > 0,\quad (P, Q')=0. \ee

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.1 (Invertibility of $L$)

nodes.statement: Note that the existence and uniqueness of $\Yz$ follows readily from standard properties of the operator $L$ (see e.g. \cite{MMR1}).

nodes.name: One parameter family of approximate self-similar profiles $Q_b$
nodes.statement: A simple consequence of Lemma \ref{lemmainvert} (ii) is the existence of a one parameter family of approximate self similar profiles $b\mapsto Q_b$, $|b|\ll 1$, which provide the leading order deformation of the ground state profile $Q=Q_{b=0}$ in the blow up regimes.
nodes.statement_short: Part (ii) of Lemma 2.1 produces the family $b\mapsto Q_b$ giving the leading-order deformation of $Q$ in the blow up regimes.

nodes.name: Cut-off $\chi_b$ and the exponent $\gamma$
nodes.statement: More precisely, let $\chi\in {\cal C}^{\infty}({\mathbb R})$ be such that $0\leq \chi \leq 1$, $\chi'\geq 0$ on $\mathbb{R}$, $\chi\equiv 1$ on $[-1,+\infty)$, $\chi\equiv 0$ on $(-\infty,-2]$, and define \begin{equation} \chi_b(y)= \chi\left(|b|^{\gamma} {y} \right),\ \ \gamma = \frac 34. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: A monotone smooth cut-off $\chi$ rescaled as $\chi_b(y)=\chi(|b|^{\gamma}y)$ with $\gamma=3/4$.

nodes.name: Approximate self-similar profile $Q_b$
nodes.statement: Let \begin{equation} \quad Q_b(y) = Q(y) + b \chi_b(y) P (y). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Approximate self-similar profiles $Q_b$
nodes.statement: Let \begin{equation} \quad Q_b(y) = Q(y) + b \chi_b(y) P (y). \end{equation} Then:\\ {\rm (i) Estimates on $Q_b$:} For all $y \in \mathbb{R}$, \begin{align} & |Q_b(y)|\lesssim e^{-|y|} + |b| \left( {\mathbf{1}}_{[-2,0]}(|b|^\gamma y) + e^{-\frac {|y|}{2}} \right), \\ & |Q_b^{(k)}(y)|\lesssim e^{-|y|} + |b| e^{-\frac {|y|}{2}} +|b|^{1+k \gamma} {\mathbf{1}}_{[-2,-1]}(|b|^\gamma y),\quad \text{for $k\geq 1$}. \end{align} \noindent {\rm (ii) Equation of $Q_b$:} let \begin{equation} -\Psi_b=\left(Q_b''- Q_b+ Q_b^5\right)'+b {\Lambda} Q_b, \end{equation} then, for all $y\in \mathbb{R}$, \begin{align} & |\Psi_b(y)|\lesssim |b|^{1+ \gamma} {\mathbf{1}}_{[-2 ,-1]}(|b|^{\gamma}y) + b^2 \left(e^{-\frac {|y|} 2}+ {\mathbf{1}}_{[- 2,0]}(|b|^{\gamma}y) \right), \\ & |\Psi_b^{(k)}(y)|\lesssim |b|^{1+ (k+1) \gamma} {\mathbf{1}}_{[-2 ,-1]}(|b|^{\gamma}y) + b^2 e^{-\frac {|y|} 2} ,\quad \text{for $k\geq 1$}. \end{align} {\rm (iii) Mass and energy properties of $Q_b$:} \begin{align} & \left|\int Q_b^2 - \left( \int Q^2 + 2b \int PQ \right)\right| \lesssim |b|^{2-\gamma}, \\ & \left| E(Q_b) + b \int PQ\right|\lesssim b^2 . \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Pointwise bounds on $Q_b$ and its derivatives, on the error $\Psi_b$ of the self-similar equation, and on the mass/energy of $Q_b$.
conclusions: {\rm (i) Estimates on $Q_b$:} For all $y \in \mathbb{R}$, \begin{align} & |Q_b(y)|\lesssim e^{-|y|} + |b| \left( {\mathbf{1}}_{[-2,0]}(|b|^\gamma y) + e^{-\frac {|y|}{2}} \right), \\ & |Q_b^{(k)}(y)|\lesssim e^{-|y|} + |b| e^{-\frac {|y|}{2}} +|b|^{1+k \gamma} {\mathbf{1}}_{[-2,-1]}(|b|^\gamma y),\quad \text{for $k\geq 1$}. \end{align}

{\rm (ii) Equation of $Q_b$:} let \begin{equation} -\Psi_b=\left(Q_b''- Q_b+ Q_b^5\right)'+b {\Lambda} Q_b, \end{equation} then, for all $y\in \mathbb{R}$, \begin{align} & |\Psi_b(y)|\lesssim |b|^{1+ \gamma} {\mathbf{1}}_{[-2 ,-1]}(|b|^{\gamma}y) + b^2 \left(e^{-\frac {|y|} 2}+ {\mathbf{1}}_{[- 2,0]}(|b|^{\gamma}y) \right), \\ & |\Psi_b^{(k)}(y)|\lesssim |b|^{1+ (k+1) \gamma} {\mathbf{1}}_{[-2 ,-1]}(|b|^{\gamma}y) + b^2 e^{-\frac {|y|} 2} ,\quad \text{for $k\geq 1$}. \end{align}

{\rm (iii) Mass and energy properties of $Q_b$:} \begin{align} & \left|\int Q_b^2 - \left( \int Q^2 + 2b \int PQ \right)\right| \lesssim |b|^{2-\gamma}, \\ & \left| E(Q_b) + b \int PQ\right|\lesssim b^2 . \end{align}

nodes.name: Slowly decaying tail $f_0$ on the right
nodes.statement: Let $c_0<0$, $x_0\gg 1$, $\theta>1$ and let $f_0$ be a smooth function such that \be f_0(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll}c_0 x^{-\theta} & \hbox{ for $x>\frac {x_0}2$},\\ 0 & \hbox{ for $x<\frac {x_0}4$,}\end{array}\right. \ee and \be \left|\frac {d^{k}f_0}{dx^k} (x)\right| \lesssim |x|^{-\theta - k}, \ \ \forall (x,k)\in \RR\times \NN. \ee
nodes.statement_short: A smooth function vanishing for $x<x_0/4$ and equal to $c_0x^{-\theta}$ for $x>x_0/2$, with all derivatives bounded by $|x|^{-\theta-k}$.

nodes.name: Free tail solution $\qz$
nodes.statement: Let $\qz$ be the solution of \be \partial_t \qz + \partial_x(\partial_x^2 \qz + \qz^5)=0,\quad \qz(0,x)= f_0(x). \ee

nodes.name: Asymptotic behavior of $\qz$
nodes.statement: The solution $\qz$ of \eqref{defqz} is global, smooth and bounded in $H^1$. Moreover, $\forall t\geq 0,\ \forall x>\frac t 2+\frac {x_0}2$, \be \forall k\geq 0,\quad |\partial_x^k \qz(t,x) -f_0^{(k)}(x) | \lesssim t^{\frac 38} x^{-\theta-\frac {19}8 - k } \lesssim x^{-\theta-2 - k }, \ee \be |\partial_t\qz(t,x) | \lesssim x^{-\theta-3} . \ee
nodes.statement_short: $\qz$ is global, smooth, $H^1$-bounded and keeps the tail of $f_0$ to all orders on the region $x>\frac t2+\frac{x_0}2$.
conclusions: The solution $\qz$ of \eqref{defqz} is global, smooth and bounded in $H^1$.

nodes.name: Reduced unknown $w=u-\qz$
nodes.statement: Let $c_0\in \RR$, $\l_0\ll 1$ and $x_0\gg 1$. Consider $u(t,x)$ a solution of \eqref{kdv} and set \be w(t,x)= u(t,x) - \qz(t,x). \ee

nodes.name: Closeness of $w$ to the soliton
nodes.statement: We assume that $w$ is close to $Q$ in the following sense : there exist $(\lambda_1(t),x_1(t))\in \RR^*_+\times \RR$ and $\e_1(t)$ such that \begin{align} \forall t\in [0,t_0], \ \ & \l_1(t)<\frac {10}9 \l_0,\quad x_1(t)> \frac 9{10} x_0, \\ & w(t,x)=\frac{1}{\lambda^{\frac 12}_1(t)}(Q+\e_1)\left(t,\frac{x-x_1(t)}{\lambda_1(t)}\right) \end{align} with \be \forall t\in [0,t_0],\ \ \|\e_1(t)\|_{L^2}+\left(\int (\partial_y \e_1)^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{2}} dy \right)^{\frac 12}\leq \alpha^* \ee for some small enough universal constant $\alpha^*>0$.
nodes.statement_short: $w$ admits a modulated decomposition $\l_1^{-1/2}(Q+\e_1)$ with $\e_1$ small in the weighted norm, on $[0,t_0]$.

nodes.statement_short: Implicit function theorem on the orthogonality map gives the decomposition; then derive the equation of $\e$, extract the conservation-law bounds, and differentiate the orthogonality conditions to get the modulation estimates.

nodes.name: step 1 -- Proof of (i), modulation by the implicit function theorem
nodes.statement: {\bf step 1} Proof of (i). This is a standard modulation claim. As usual, the decomposition is first performed for a fixed time $t$. For $t\in [0,t_0]$ fixed, define the map $$ \Theta: (\bar b,\bar \l,\bar x,w,z_0) \mapsto \left( \int Q\bar \e , \int \Lambda Q \bar \e ,\int Q' \bar \e \right), $$ where $x_0=1/z_0$, $$ \bar \e(y)=\e_{(\bar b,{\bar \l},\bar x,w_1,z_0)}(y) = {\bar \l}^{\frac 12} w_1\left(t, {\bar \l} y + \bar x\right) - {\bar \l}^{\frac 12} {\l_1^{\frac 12}(t)} q_0\left(t,x_1(t) + \bar x\right)\Yz(y)- Q_{\bar b}(y), $$ $$ w_1(t,y)= { \l_1(t)}^{\frac 12} w \left(t, {\l_1(t)} y + x_1(t)\right)=Q(y)+\e_1(t,y). $$ We have $\bar \e|_{(0,1,0,Q,0)}=0,$ so that $\Theta(0,1,0,Q,0)=0$ and $$ \quad \partial_{\bar b} \bar \e |_{(0,1,0,Q,0)}= P, \quad \partial_{\bar \l} \bar \e|_{(0,1,0,Q,0)}= \Lambda Q, \quad \partial_{\bar x} \bar \e|_{(0,1,0,Q,0)}= Q'. $$ so that differentiating the map $\Theta$ with respect to the variables $(\bar b,\bar \l,\bar x)$ at the point $(0,1,0,Q,0)$ we find the Jacobian matrix $$ \left(\begin{array}{ ccc } (P,Q) & (P,\Lambda Q) & (P,Q') \\ (\Lambda Q,Q) & (\Lambda Q,\Lambda Q) & (\Lambda Q,Q') \\ (Q',Q) & (Q',\lambda Q) & (Q',Q')\\ \end{array}\right)= \left(\begin{array}{ ccc } (P,Q) & (P,\Lambda Q) & 0\\0 & (\Lambda Q,\Lambda Q) &0 \\ 0 & 0 & (Q',Q')\\ \end{array}\right), $$ which is not degenerate since $(P,Q)>0$. It follows from these observations that we can apply the implicit function theorem to $\Theta$: for $w_1$ small and $x_0$ large, there exists a unique $(\bar b ,\bar \l , \bar x)=(\bar b ,\bar \l , \bar x)(w_1,x_0)$ close to $(0,1,0)$ such that $\Theta(\bar b,\bar \l,\bar x,w_1,\tfrac 1{x_0})=0$. Then, we define $b(t)=\bar b(w_1(t),x_0)$, $\l(t)=\bar \l(w_1(t),x_0) \l_1(t)$, $x(t)=\bar x(w_1(t),x_0)+x_1(t)$ and $\e(t)=\bar \e(t)$. The regularity of $(b(t),\l(t),x(t))$ now follow from standard arguments. It follows that we have the following decomposition of $u(t,x)$: \begin{align} u(t,x) & = \frac 1{\l^{\frac 12}(t)} \left( Q_{b(t)} + p(t) \Yz+ \e \right) \left( t,\frac {x-x(t)}{\l(t)}\right) +q_0(t,x) \\ & = \frac 1{\l^{\frac 12}(t)} \left( Q_{b(t)} + p(t) \Yz+ \e + q \right) \left(t, \frac {x-x(t)}{\l(t)}\right). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Build the map $\Theta$ of the three orthogonality conditions, compute its non-degenerate Jacobian using $(P,Q)>0$, and apply the implicit function theorem.

nodes.name: step 2 -- Equation of $\e$ and a priori bounds
nodes.statement_short: Derive the equations of $w$, of $\e_Y$ and finally of $\e$, and prove Claim 1 collecting the estimates on $q$, $p$ and $W$.

nodes.name: step 3 -- Estimates induced by the conservation laws
nodes.statement: {\bf step 3} Estimates induced by the conservation laws. By $L^2$ norm conservation, \begin{align*} & \int u^2(0) - \int Q^2 = \int Q_b^2 - \int Q^2 + \int (\e+p\Yz+q)^2 + 2 \int (\e+p\Yz +q) Q_b\\ &= 2 b(P,Q) + O(|b|^{2-\gamma}) +\|\e\|_{L^2}^2 + O(|b|^{1-\frac \gamma 2}\|\e\|_{L^2}) +O(|p|+ \|q\|_{L^2}). \end{align*} Estimate \eqref{twobound} follows. By energy conservation, $Q''+Q^5= Q$ and $\int \e Q=0$, \begin{align*} & 2 \l^2 E(u_0) = 2 E(Q_b + \e + p\Yz +q) \\& = 2 E(Q_b) - 2 \int (\e+p\Yz + q) \left( (Q_b-Q)_{yy}+ (Q_b^5 - Q^5) \right) - 2 \int (p\Yz + q) Q \\ &+ \int (\e+p\Yz + q)_y^2 - \frac 13 \int \left( (Q_b+\e+p\Yz + q)^6 - Q_b^6 - 6 Q_b^5(\e+pY+q)\right)\\ & = - 2 b (P,Q) + O(b^2) + O\left( |b|^{1+\frac 32 \gamma} \left( \|\e\|_{L^2} + |p| + \|q\|_{L^2}\right)\right) - 2 p \left( \int \Yz Q + \int Q\right) \\ &+ 2 \int (p-q) Q + \|\e_y\|_{L^2}^2 + O(p^2) + O\left(\|\e_y\|_{L^2}(|p|+ \|q_y\|_{L^2})\right) + 2\l^2 E(q_0) \\ &- \frac 13 \int \left( (Q_b+\e+p\Yz+q)^6 - Q_b^6 - 6Q_b^5 (\e+p\Yz+q) -q^6\right) \end{align*} By \eqref{YQ}, we have $\int \Yz Q + \int Q = \frac 14 \int Q$. Using in addition \eqref{PQ}, \eqref{cl.2}, \eqref{cl.1bis}, we obtain \begin{align*} \frac 1{\l^2}\|\e_y\|_{L^2}^2 & \lesssim |E(u_0)| + \left| \frac 14 \frac b{\l^2} \int Q + \frac p{\l^2}\right| + \frac {b^2}{\l^2}+ \frac {|b|^{1+\frac 32 \gamma}}{\l^2} \left( \|\e\|_{L^2} + |p| + \|q\|_{L^2}\right) \\ & + \frac { |p| }{\l x} + \frac {p^2}{\l^2} + x_0^{-\theta-\frac 12}\\ & \lesssim |E(u_0)| + \left| \frac 14 \frac b{\l^2} \int Q + c_0 \l^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta} \right| + \frac {b^2}{\l^2}+ \frac { |p| }{x^2} + \frac { |p| }{\l x} + \frac {p^2}{\l^2} + x_0^{-\theta-\frac 12} . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Expand the conserved mass and energy in the decomposition to bound $\|\e\|_{L^2}$ and $\l^{-1}\|\e_y\|_{L^2}$.

nodes.name: step 4 -- Modulation equations
nodes.statement:
{ f step 4} Modulation equations. We argue as in \cite{MMR1}, proof of Lemma 2.7, differentiating with respect to $s$ the orthogonality conditions $\int \e \Lambda Q=0$, $\int \e Q'=0$ and $\int \e Q=0$ and using \eqref{eqofeps} to obtain \eqref{eq:2002bis} and \eqref{eq:2003}. Here, we will treat only the terms coming from $q$ and $p\Yz$ in \eqref{eqofeps} and we refer the reader to \cite{MMR1} for more details on the other terms. \medskip \emph{Proof of \eqref{eq:2002bis} and \eqref{eq:2003}.} It follows from computations in \cite{MMR1} proof of Lemma~2.7 and Claim ef{cl:one} that  egin{align*} & \left| \left( { rac{{\lambda}_s}{{\lambda}}} + {b} ight) -  rac {( \e,L(\Lambda Q)')}{\|\Lambda Q\|_{L^2}^2} ight| \ & \lesssim \left( \left| { rac{{\lambda}_s}{{\lambda}}}+ {b} ight| +|b|ight)\left(|p|+ |b| + \left( \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} ight)^{ rac 12} ight) + |p| \left( \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} ight)^{ rac 12} \ & + \left| { rac{x_s}{{\lambda}}} - 1 ight| \left( |b| + \left( \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} ight)^{ rac 12} ight) +|p_s|+|{b}_{s}|+\int \varepsilon^2 e^{- rac{|y|}{10}} + p^8 +  rac {\l}{x} |p| . \end{align*} We proceed similarly for $\xsl-1$, taking into account different cancellations due to parity properties  egin{align*} & \left|\left( { rac{x_s}{{\lambda}}} - 1 ight) -  rac {( \e,L(y \Lambda Q)')}{\|\Lambda Q\|_{L^2}^2} ight| \ & \lesssim \left( \left| { rac{{\lambda}_s}{{\lambda}}}+ {b} ight| + \left| { rac{x_s}{{\lambda}}} - 1 ight| +|b|ight)\left(|p|+|b| + \left( \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} ight)^{ rac 12} ight) \ &+|{b}_{s}|+\int \varepsilon^2 e^{- rac{|y|}{10}} +p^2 + rac \l x |p|. \end{align*} Then, taking the scalar product of \eqref{eqofeps} by $Q$ and arguing similarly, we have the following rough estimate for $b_s$:  egin{align*} |{b}_{s}| &\lesssim \left| { rac{{\lambda}_s}{{\lambda}}} + {b}ight|^2 + \left| { rac{x_s}{{\lambda}}} - 1 ight|^2 + {|b|}^2 + \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} + |p| \left( \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} ight)^{ rac 12} \ &+|p_s| + |b| |p| +p^8 + rac \l x |p| . \end{align*} Combining these estimates with (from \eqref{cl.2bis}) $$ |p_s| \leq \left| \lsl ight| |p| +  rac {\l}{x} |p|\left( \left|\xsl - 1ight| + 1 ight) \leq |b| |p| +\left| \lsl+bight| |p| +  rac \l x |p|\left( \left|\xsl - 1ight| + 1 ight), $$ from \eqref{cl.2tri}, we obtain \eqref{eq:2002bis} and \eqref{eq:2003}. \medskip \emph{Proof of \eqref{fond}.} First, we derive a refined equation for $b_s$, taking the scalar product of equation \eqref{eqofeps} by $Q$ and proceeding as in \cite{MMR1}, proof of Lemma 2.7. Recall from \cite{MMR1}, $$(\Psi_b,Q)= - rac {b^2}{8} \|Q\|_{L^1}^2 + O(|b|^3),\quad (\Phi_b, Q) = - rac {b_s}{16} \|Q\|_{L^1}^2 +O(|b|^{10}). $$ Note also that from direct computations and parity properties  egin{align*} &\left|\left( ((\e+p\Yz + Q_b)^5 - Q_b^5 - p5Q^4 \Yz - 5Q^4 \e)_y,Qight) - 20 bp((Q^3\Yz P )_y,Q) ight| \ &+ \left| \left((\widetilde W)_y,Qight)-20 bp (( P Q^3)_y,Q)ight|\ & \lesssim |b|^3 +|p|^3 + \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} + (|p|+|b|) \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} ight)^{ rac 12} . \end{align*} (See \cite{MMR1} for details on the nonlinear terms in $\e$.) Using \eqref{cl.4bis} and the above estimates we find egin{align} & igg| b_s + 2b^2 -  rac {16}{(\int Q)^2}  igg( - p_s (\Yz,Q) - \lsl p (\Yz,\Lambda Q) 
onumber\ & - bp \left[ 20 ((Q^3\Yz P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) ight] + c_0 	heta \left(\int Qight) \l^{ rac 32}(s) x^{-	heta-1}(s)  igg) igg|\ & \lesssim |b|^3+ |p|^3 +\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} +(|p|+|b|) \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} ight)^{ rac 12} + rac {\l^2}{x^2} |p|+ rac {\l}{x^3} |p|. \end{align} We claim the following cancellation  e - (\Yz,\Lambda Q) + 20 ((Q^3\Yz P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) =0. \ee Indeed, $L(P')= (LP)' + 20 Q^3 Q' P = \Lambda Q + 20 Q^3 Q' P,$ and so from \eqref{eq:23},  egin{align*} & - (\Yz,\Lambda Q) + 20 ((Q^3\Yz P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) \ &= - (\Yz,\Lambda Q)- 20 (\Yz+1,PQ^3 Q')\ & = - (\Yz+1 , L(P')) + \int \Lambda Q = - (L(\Yz+1),P') -  rac 12 \int Q \ & = - \int P' -  rac 12 \int Q = P(-\infty) -  rac 12 \int Q =0. \end{align*} Thus,  egin{align*} & \left| - \lsl p (\Yz,\Lambda Q) + bp \left[ 20 ((Q^3\Yz P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) ight] ight| = |p| \left| \lsl+b ight| |(\Yz,\Lambda Q)|. \end{align*} \medskip Now, from $(\Yz,Q) =-  rac 34 \int Q$ (see \eqref{YQ}), using \eqref{cl.1bis} and \eqref{cl.2bis} we note that  egin{align} &  rac {16}{(\int Q)^2}  igg( - p_s (\Yz,Q)+ c_0 	heta \left(\int Qight) \l^{ rac 32}(s) x^{-	heta-1}(s)  igg)
onumber \ & =  rac {12}{(\int Q)} c_0 \l^{ rac 12} x^{-	heta} \left(  rac 12 \lsl + rac 	heta 3  rac {x_s}{x} ight) +O\left( rac {\l}{x^{3}}| p|ight) + O\left(  rac {\l}{x} |p| \left|\xsl-1ight|ight). \end{align} Therefore,  egin{align} & igg| b_s + 2b^2 -  rac {4}{(\int Q)} c_0 \l^{ rac 12} x^{-	heta} \left(  rac 32 \lsl + 	heta  rac {x_s}{x} ight)  igg| 
onumber \ & \lesssim |b|^3 +|p|^3 + \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} + (|p|+|b|) \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} ight)^{ rac 12} +  rac {\l^2}{x^2} |p| +  rac {\l}{x^3} |p| . \end{align} Now, we prove \eqref{fond}. By direct computation, $$  rac d{ds}\left(  rac 4{\left(\int Qight)}c_0 	heta \l^{- rac 32}(s) x^{-	heta}ight) = -  rac {4}{(\int Q)} c_0 \l^{- rac 32} x^{-	heta} \left(  rac 32 \lsl + 	heta  rac {x_s}{x} ight) $$ $$  rac d{ds}\left(  rac b{\l^2}ight) =  rac {b_s}{\l^2} - 2 \lsl  rac b{\l^2} =  rac {b_s}{\l^2} + 2  rac {b^2}{\l^2} - 2 \left( \lsl +bight)  rac b{\l^2}.$$ and \eqref{fond} follows from \eqref{eq:b} and \eqref{eq:2002bis}.
nodes.statement_short: Take scalar products of the $\e$-equation with $\Lambda Q$, $y\Lambda Q$ and $Q$, use the cancellation \eqref{cancel}, and reorganize into the law of $b/\l^2$.

nodes.name: Equation of the remainder $\e$
nodes.statement: Finally, we replace $ \e(s,y) = \e_Y(s,y)- p(s) \Yz(y) $ and use $L \Yz = 5 Q^4 $, to obtain \begin{align} \nonumber \partial_s \varepsilon & = \left(-\partial_{y}^2 \e + \e - (\e +p \Yz +Q_b)^5 +Q_b^5 + p5Q^4 \Yz\right)_y \\ & -p_s \Yz +( 5 Q^4 (p-q) )_y +\lsl (\Lambda \e+p\Lambda \Yz) + \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) {\Lambda} Q_b \nonumber \\ &+ \left(\frac { x_{s}}{\lambda} -1\right) (Q_b + \varepsilon+p \Yz)_y + \Phi_{b} + \Psi_{{b}} -W_y, \end{align} and \begin{align*} W&=5(Q_b+ \e+p \Yz)^4 q- 5 Q^4 q + 10(Q_b+\e+p \Yz)^3 q^2 \\ &+ 10(Q_b+\e+p \Yz)^2 q^3 + 5(Q_b+\e+p \Yz) q^4. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Evolution equation for $\e$ with the tail forcing $(5Q^4(p-q))_y$, the modulation terms and the errors $\Phi_b$, $\Psi_b$, $W_y$.

nodes.name: Estimates on $q$, $p$ and the remainder term $W$
nodes.statement: {\rm (a) Estimates on $q(s)$.} \be \|q(s)\|_{L^2} \lesssim x_0^{-\theta+\frac 12}, \quad \|q_y(s)\|_{L^2}\lesssim \l(s) x_0^{-\theta-\frac 12}, \quad \|q(s)\|_{L^\infty}\lesssim \l^{\frac 12} (s) x_0^{-\theta}. \ee {\rm (b) Properties of the function $p(s)$:} \be \left|p(s) - c_0 \l^{\frac 12}(s) x^{-\theta}(s)\right| \lesssim c_0 \l^{\frac 12}(s) x^{-\theta-2}(s)\lesssim x^{-2}(s) |p(s)|, \ee \be e^{-\frac{3|y|}{4}} |p(s)-q(s,y)| \lesssim \frac {\l(s)}{x(s)} |p(s)| e^{-\frac {|y|} 4} , \ee \be \left| \left( (5Q^4(p-q))_y ,Q\right) - c_0 \left( \int Q\right) \theta \l^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta-1} \right| \lesssim \frac {\l^2(s)}{x^2(s)} |p(s)|+\frac {\l(s)}{x^3(s)} |p(s)|, \ee \be \left| p_s - \frac 12 \lsl p + \theta \frac {x_s} x p \right| \leq \frac {\l}{x^{3}}|p| \left(\left|\xsl - 1\right| + 1 \right), \ee \be |p_s| \lesssim \left| \lsl\right| |p| + \frac {\l}{x} |p| \left(\left|\xsl - 1\right| + 1 \right). \ee {\rm (c) Estimates for the remainder term $W$:} Let \begin{align*} \widetilde W&=5(Q_b+ \e+p \Yz)^4 p- 5 Q^4 p + 10(Q_b+\e+p \Yz)^3 p^2 \\ &+ 10(Q_b+\e+p \Yz)^2 p^3 + 5(Q_b+\e+p \Yz) p^4. \end{align*} Then, \be \int |W-\widetilde W| e^{-\frac 34 {|y|}} \lesssim \left( |p|+|b| + \left( \int \e^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} \right)^{\frac 12}\right) \frac {\l}{x} |p| , \ee \be |((\widetilde W)_y,\Lambda Q)|+|((\widetilde W)_y,Q)|\lesssim b^2 + p^8 +|b| |p| +|p| \left(\int \e^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}}\right)^{\frac 12} +\int \e^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} , \ee \be |((\widetilde W)_y,y \Lambda Q)| \lesssim \int \e^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} + b^2 + p^2. \ee
nodes.statement_short: Weighted bounds on the renormalized tail $q$, the almost-explicit law of $p\simeq c_0\l^{1/2}x^{-\theta}$, and control of the nonlinear tail interaction $W$.
assumptions: Assume \fref{decompo0}--\fref{hypeprochien} for $\alpha^*$ small enough, and assume $x_0$ large enough and $\l_0$ small enough.
conclusions: {\rm (a) Estimates on $q(s)$.} \be \|q(s)\|_{L^2} \lesssim x_0^{-\theta+\frac 12}, \quad \|q_y(s)\|_{L^2}\lesssim \l(s) x_0^{-\theta-\frac 12}, \quad \|q(s)\|_{L^\infty}\lesssim \l^{\frac 12} (s) x_0^{-\theta}. \ee

{\rm (b) Properties of the function $p(s)$:} \be \left|p(s) - c_0 \l^{\frac 12}(s) x^{-\theta}(s)\right| \lesssim c_0 \l^{\frac 12}(s) x^{-\theta-2}(s)\lesssim x^{-2}(s) |p(s)|, \ee \be e^{-\frac{3|y|}{4}} |p(s)-q(s,y)| \lesssim \frac {\l(s)}{x(s)} |p(s)| e^{-\frac {|y|} 4} , \ee \be \left| \left( (5Q^4(p-q))_y ,Q\right) - c_0 \left( \int Q\right) \theta \l^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta-1} \right| \lesssim \frac {\l^2(s)}{x^2(s)} |p(s)|+\frac {\l(s)}{x^3(s)} |p(s)|, \ee \be \left| p_s - \frac 12 \lsl p + \theta \frac {x_s} x p \right| \leq \frac {\l}{x^{3}}|p| \left(\left|\xsl - 1\right| + 1 \right), \ee \be |p_s| \lesssim \left| \lsl\right| |p| + \frac {\l}{x} |p| \left(\left|\xsl - 1\right| + 1 \right). \ee

{\rm (c) Estimates for the remainder term $W$:} Let \begin{align*} \widetilde W&=5(Q_b+ \e+p \Yz)^4 p- 5 Q^4 p + 10(Q_b+\e+p \Yz)^3 p^2 \\ &+ 10(Q_b+\e+p \Yz)^2 p^3 + 5(Q_b+\e+p \Yz) p^4. \end{align*} Then, \be \int |W-\widetilde W| e^{-\frac 34 {|y|}} \lesssim \left( |p|+|b| + \left( \int \e^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} \right)^{\frac 12}\right) \frac {\l}{x} |p| , \ee \be |((\widetilde W)_y,\Lambda Q)|+|((\widetilde W)_y,Q)|\lesssim b^2 + p^8 +|b| |p| +|p| \left(\int \e^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}}\right)^{\frac 12} +\int \e^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} , \ee \be |((\widetilde W)_y,y \Lambda Q)| \lesssim \int \e^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} + b^2 + p^2. \ee

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 1
nodes.statement:
{\it Proof of} (a). Since $q_0(t)$ is solution of \eqref{kdv}, for all $t$, $$ \|q_0(t)\|_{L^2}= \|f_0\|_{L^2} \lesssim x_0^{-	heta+ rac 12},\quad E(q_0(t)) = E(f_0) \lesssim x_0^{-	heta-  rac 12}, $$ and \eqref{L2H1q} follows.\ {\it Proof of} (b). Since $p(s) = \lambda^{ rac 12}(s) q_0(s,x(s))$, \eqref{cl.1bis} follows from \eqref{surX} and \eqref{leqz3}. In particular, since $c_0<0$, $p<0$. Next, by \eqref{surX}, \eqref{leqz3} and \eqref{estfz}, splitting the two cases $\l |y|< rac {x(s)}{4}$ and $\l |y| >  rac {x(s)}{4}$, we have  egin{align} & e^{- rac{3|y|}{4}} |p(s)-q(s,y)| = e^{- rac{3|y|}{4}} \l^{ rac 12}(s) |q_0(s,x(s))-q_0(s,\l(s) y +x(s))| 
onumber\ &\lesssim |y| e^{-  rac {|y|} 2 } \l^{ rac 32}(s) \left( e^{-  rac { |y|} 4} \|q_0'(s)\|_{L^\infty(x> rac 34 x(s))} + e^{- rac {x(s)}{16\l(s)}}\|q_0'(s)\|_{L^\infty} ight)
onumber \ & \lesssim c_0 e^{- rac {|y|} 4} \l^{ rac 32}(s) \left( x^{-	heta-1}(s) + e^{- rac {x(s)}{16\l(s)}} x_0^{-	heta-1} ight)
onumber \ &\lesssim c_0 e^{- rac {|y|} 4} \l^{ rac 32}(s) x^{-	heta-1}(s) \lesssim  rac {\l}{x} |p| e^{- rac {|y|} 4}.\end{align} Next, by \eqref{surX} and \eqref{leqz3},  egin{align*} &\left( (5Q^4(p-q))_y ,Qight) = -5 \int Q^4 Q_y (p-q)= -\int Q^5 q_y \ &= -\l^{ rac 32}(s) \int Q^5(y) \partial_x q_0(s,\l(s) y +x(s)) dy\ &= - \l^{ rac 32} f_0'( x(s)) \int Q^5 - \l^{ rac 32} \int Q^5 \left(f_0'(\l y + x(s)) -f_0'(x(s))ight)dy \ & -\l^{ rac 32}(s) \int Q^5(y) \left( \partial_x q_0(s,\l(s) y +x(s) )-f_0'(\l y+x(s))ight) dy\ & =c_0 \left( \int Qight) 	heta \l^{ rac 32}(s) x^{-	heta -1}(s) + O\left( \l^{ rac 32}e^{- rac 54 x(s) } ight) + O\left( \l^{ rac 52} x^{-	heta-2}ight) +O\left( \l^{ rac 32} x^{-	heta-3}(s)ight)\ & =c_0 \left( \int Qight) 	heta \l^{ rac 32}(s) x^{-	heta -1}(s) + O\left( rac {\l^2}{x^2} |p| ight) + O\left( rac {\l}{x^3} |p| ight), \end{align*} where we have split the integrals above into $|y| > rac 14 x(s)$ and $|y|< rac 14 x(s)$ and using the fact that for $|y|< rac 14 x(s)$, $\l y + x(s) >x(s)-|y|>  rac 34 x(s) >  rac 12 t +  rac 12 x_0$, so that \eqref{leqz3} holds for $x= \l y + x(s)$, and  ref{cl.4bis} is proved.\ Now, we prove \eqref{cl.2bis}. By explicit differentiation and Lemma ef{le:qz},  egin{align*} p_s -  rac 12 \lsl p & = \l^{ rac 12}(q_0)_s(s,x(s)) + \l^{ rac 12} x_s \partial_x q_0(s,x(s))\ & = \l^{ rac 72} (q_0)_t(s,x(s)) + \l^{ rac 12} x_s f_0'(x(s)) + O\left(  rac {\l}{x^{3}} |p| \left(\left|\xsl - 1ight| + 1 ight) ight)\ & = -	heta  rac {x_s} x |p| + O\left(  rac {\l}{x^{3}} |p| \left(\left|\xsl - 1ight| + 1 ight) ight). \end{align*} Since $|x_s| \leq \l (|\xsl -1| + 1)$, \eqref{cl.2tri} follows.\ {\it Proof of} (c). For \eqref{cl.3}, we first note  egin{align*} \widetilde W - W &=5\left[(Q_b+ \e+p \Yz)^4 - Q^4ight] (p-q) + 10(Q_b+\e+p \Yz)^3 (p^2-q^2) \ &+ 10(Q_b+\e+p \Yz)^2 (p^3-q^3) + 5(Q_b+\e+p \Yz) (p^4-q^4). \end{align*} Thus,  egin{align*} & \int e^{- rac 34 {|y|}} |W-\widetilde W| \ &\lesssim \left( |p|+|b| ight) \int e^{-  rac 34 {|y|}} |p-q| + \left( \int \e^2 e^{- rac {|y|}{10}} ight)^{ rac 12}\left( \int e^{-( rac 32- rac 1{10}) {|y|}} |p-q|^2ight)^{ rac 12} \ & + \int e^{- rac 34 {|y|}} |p^2-q^2| \lesssim \left( |p|+|b| + \left( \int \e^2 e^{- rac {|y|}{10}} ight)^{ rac 12}ight)  rac {\l}{x}|p|, \end{align*} using \eqref{cl.2}, and the following similar estimate $$ e^{- rac 34 {|y|}} |p^2-q^2| \lesssim  rac {\l}{x} p^2 e^{- rac {|y|}{4}}. $$ Next, \eqref{cl.4} follows from the parity properties and then direct estimates. \eqref{cl.5} follows from direct estimates. Note that $p^2$ appears in \eqref{cl.5} because there is no cancellation due to parity for this term. This concludes the proof of Claim ef{cl:one}.
nodes.statement_short: Use conservation of mass/energy for $q_0$ for (a), the tail asymptotics of Lemma 2.3 plus a split of the integration region for (b), and parity plus direct estimates for (c).

nodes.name: Proof of (a) -- estimates on $q(s)$
nodes.statement: {\it Proof of} (a). Since $q_0(t)$ is solution of \eqref{kdv}, for all $t$, $$ \|q_0(t)\|_{L^2}= \|f_0\|_{L^2} \lesssim x_0^{-\theta+\frac 12},\quad E(q_0(t)) = E(f_0) \lesssim x_0^{-\theta- \frac 12}, $$ and \eqref{L2H1q} follows.
nodes.statement_short: Conservation of mass and energy for $q_0$ gives the three weighted norms of $q$.

nodes.name: Proof of (b) -- properties of $p(s)$
nodes.statement:
{\it Proof of} (b). Since $p(s) = \lambda^{ rac 12}(s) q_0(s,x(s))$, \eqref{cl.1bis} follows from \eqref{surX} and \eqref{leqz3}. In particular, since $c_0<0$, $p<0$. Next, by \eqref{surX}, \eqref{leqz3} and \eqref{estfz}, splitting the two cases $\l |y|< rac {x(s)}{4}$ and $\l |y| >  rac {x(s)}{4}$, we have  egin{align} & e^{- rac{3|y|}{4}} |p(s)-q(s,y)| = e^{- rac{3|y|}{4}} \l^{ rac 12}(s) |q_0(s,x(s))-q_0(s,\l(s) y +x(s))| 
onumber\ &\lesssim |y| e^{-  rac {|y|} 2 } \l^{ rac 32}(s) \left( e^{-  rac { |y|} 4} \|q_0'(s)\|_{L^\infty(x> rac 34 x(s))} + e^{- rac {x(s)}{16\l(s)}}\|q_0'(s)\|_{L^\infty} ight)
onumber \ & \lesssim c_0 e^{- rac {|y|} 4} \l^{ rac 32}(s) \left( x^{-	heta-1}(s) + e^{- rac {x(s)}{16\l(s)}} x_0^{-	heta-1} ight)
onumber \ &\lesssim c_0 e^{- rac {|y|} 4} \l^{ rac 32}(s) x^{-	heta-1}(s) \lesssim  rac {\l}{x} |p| e^{- rac {|y|} 4}.\end{align} Next, by \eqref{surX} and \eqref{leqz3},  egin{align*} &\left( (5Q^4(p-q))_y ,Qight) = -5 \int Q^4 Q_y (p-q)= -\int Q^5 q_y \ &= -\l^{ rac 32}(s) \int Q^5(y) \partial_x q_0(s,\l(s) y +x(s)) dy\ &= - \l^{ rac 32} f_0'( x(s)) \int Q^5 - \l^{ rac 32} \int Q^5 \left(f_0'(\l y + x(s)) -f_0'(x(s))ight)dy \ & -\l^{ rac 32}(s) \int Q^5(y) \left( \partial_x q_0(s,\l(s) y +x(s) )-f_0'(\l y+x(s))ight) dy\ & =c_0 \left( \int Qight) 	heta \l^{ rac 32}(s) x^{-	heta -1}(s) + O\left( \l^{ rac 32}e^{- rac 54 x(s) } ight) + O\left( \l^{ rac 52} x^{-	heta-2}ight) +O\left( \l^{ rac 32} x^{-	heta-3}(s)ight)\ & =c_0 \left( \int Qight) 	heta \l^{ rac 32}(s) x^{-	heta -1}(s) + O\left( rac {\l^2}{x^2} |p| ight) + O\left( rac {\l}{x^3} |p| ight), \end{align*} where we have split the integrals above into $|y| > rac 14 x(s)$ and $|y|< rac 14 x(s)$ and using the fact that for $|y|< rac 14 x(s)$, $\l y + x(s) >x(s)-|y|>  rac 34 x(s) >  rac 12 t +  rac 12 x_0$, so that \eqref{leqz3} holds for $x= \l y + x(s)$, and  ref{cl.4bis} is proved.\ Now, we prove \eqref{cl.2bis}. By explicit differentiation and Lemma ef{le:qz},  egin{align*} p_s -  rac 12 \lsl p & = \l^{ rac 12}(q_0)_s(s,x(s)) + \l^{ rac 12} x_s \partial_x q_0(s,x(s))\ & = \l^{ rac 72} (q_0)_t(s,x(s)) + \l^{ rac 12} x_s f_0'(x(s)) + O\left(  rac {\l}{x^{3}} |p| \left(\left|\xsl - 1ight| + 1 ight) ight)\ & = -	heta  rac {x_s} x |p| + O\left(  rac {\l}{x^{3}} |p| \left(\left|\xsl - 1ight| + 1 ight) ight). \end{align*} Since $|x_s| \leq \l (|\xsl -1| + 1)$, \eqref{cl.2tri} follows.
nodes.statement_short: Split $\l|y|$ small/large and use the tail asymptotics to get $p\simeq c_0\l^{1/2}x^{-\theta}$, the $p-q$ bound, the scalar product identity and the law of $p_s$.

nodes.name: Proof of (c) -- estimates for the remainder term $W$
nodes.statement: {\it Proof of} (c). For \eqref{cl.3}, we first note \begin{align*} \widetilde W - W &=5\left[(Q_b+ \e+p \Yz)^4 - Q^4\right] (p-q) + 10(Q_b+\e+p \Yz)^3 (p^2-q^2) \\ &+ 10(Q_b+\e+p \Yz)^2 (p^3-q^3) + 5(Q_b+\e+p \Yz) (p^4-q^4). \end{align*} Thus, \begin{align*} & \int e^{-\frac 34 {|y|}} |W-\widetilde W| \\ &\lesssim \left( |p|+|b| \right) \int e^{- \frac 34 {|y|}} |p-q| + \left( \int \e^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} \right)^{\frac 12}\left( \int e^{-(\frac 32-\frac 1{10}) {|y|}} |p-q|^2\right)^{\frac 12} \\ & + \int e^{-\frac 34 {|y|}} |p^2-q^2| \lesssim \left( |p|+|b| + \left( \int \e^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} \right)^{\frac 12}\right) \frac {\l}{x}|p|, \end{align*} using \eqref{cl.2}, and the following similar estimate $$ e^{-\frac 34 {|y|}} |p^2-q^2| \lesssim \frac {\l}{x} p^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{4}}. $$ Next, \eqref{cl.4} follows from the parity properties and then direct estimates. \eqref{cl.5} follows from direct estimates. Note that $p^2$ appears in \eqref{cl.5} because there is no cancellation due to parity for this term. This concludes the proof of Claim \ref{cl:one}.
nodes.statement_short: Compare $W$ with its frozen version $\widetilde W$ term by term and use parity to bound the scalar products.

nodes.name: Parameters $\beta$, $\theta$ and $c_0$
nodes.statement: Let $$ \beta = \frac { 2(\theta-1)} {2\theta-1},\quad \theta = \frac {1-\frac \beta2}{1-\beta}, \quad 0< \beta< \frac {11}{20}, \quad 1<\theta <\frac {29}{18},$$ and define \be c_0=-\frac {\int Q}2(\theta-1)(2\theta-1)^{\theta-1}. \ee
nodes.statement_short: The tail exponent $\theta$ and the amplitude $c_0$ are tied to the scaling law exponent $\beta\in(0,11/20)$.

nodes.name: Instability functionals $g(s)$ and $f(s)$
nodes.statement: Given $s>s_0$, $(b(s),\l(s),x(s))\in \RR^*_+\times \RR^*_+\times \RR$, we define: $$ g(s) =\frac {b(s)}{\l^2(s)} + \frac 4{\int Q} c_0 \l^{-\frac 32}(s) x^{-\theta}(s),\quad f(s) = \l^{\frac 12} (s) + \frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1} {x^{-\theta+1}(s)}. $$
nodes.statement_short: The two quantities whose vanishing encodes the two unstable directions $\ell_0=\ell_1=0$.

nodes.name: Weight functions $\varphi_i$, $\psi$, $\varphi_{i,B}$, $\psi_B$
nodes.statement: Let $(\varphi_i)_{i=1,2},\psi$ be smooth functions such that: \bea \varphi_i(y) =\left\{\begin{array}{lll}e^{y}\ \ \mbox{for} \ \ y<-1,\\ 1+y \ \ \mbox{for}\ \ -\frac 12<y<\frac 12,\\ y^i\ \ \mbox{for}\ \ \mbox{for}\ \ y>2, \end{array}\right. \ \ \varphi_i'(y) >0, \ \ \forall y\in \RR, \eea \bea \psi(y) =\left\{\begin{array}{ll} e^{2y}\ \ \mbox{for} \ \ y<-1,\\ 1 \ \ \mbox{for}\ \ y>-\tfrac 12,\end{array}\right. \ \ \psi'(y) \geq 0 \ \ \forall y\in \RR. \eea Let $B> 100$ and $$\psi_B(y)=\psi\left(\frac yB\right), \ \ \varphi_{i,B}=\varphi_i\left(\frac yB\right), \ \ i=1,2,$$
nodes.statement_short: Monotone weights that are exponential on the left and polynomial of degree $i$ on the right, rescaled by the large parameter $B$.

nodes.name: Adapted norms $\mathcal N_i$ and $\mathcal N_{i,\rm loc}$
nodes.statement: and define the following norms on $\e$ \begin{equation} {\mathcal{N}_i} (s) = \int \varepsilon_y^2(s,y) \psi_{B}(y)dy + \int \varepsilon^2(s,y) \varphi_{i,B}(y) dy, \end{equation} \be {\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}} (s) = \int\varepsilon^2 (s,y) \varphi'_{i,B} (y) dy,\quad i=1,2. \ee

nodes.name: Bootstrap
nodes.statement: Let $s_0=s_0(\beta)>1$ large enough and set \be x_0= x (s_0)= \frac 1{(1-\beta)}{s_0^{1-\beta}}. \ee Let $\e_0\in H^1$ be such that \be s_0^{10}\left[ \int_{y>0} y^{10} \e^2_0(y) dy+\|\e_0\|^2_{H^1} \right]<1, \quad (\e_0, y {\Lambda} Q )=(\e_0,\Lambda Q) =(\e_0,Q)=0.\ee Then, there exists \be (\l_0,b_0)\in\mathcal D =\left \{(\l,b) \ : \ | \l - s_0^{-\beta}| \leq s_0^{-\beta - \frac 1{10}}, \ |b - \beta s_0^{-1}| \leq s_0^{-1-\frac 1{10}}\right\}, \ee such that the solution of \eqref{kdv} with initial data \be u_0(x) = \frac 1{\l^{\frac 12}_0} \left( Q_{b_0} + \l^{\frac 12}_0 q_0(s_0,x_0) \Yz+ \e_0 \right) \left( \frac {x-x_0}{\l_0}\right) +q_0(s_0,x) \ee has a decomposition $(b(s),\l(s),x(s), \e(s))$ as in Proposition \ref{le:2} which satisfies\footnote{recall that $s=s(t)$ is the rescaled time \fref{rescaledtime}.} on $[s_0,+\infty)$: $$\leqno{\rm (BS1)}\quad \left(|g(s)| s^{1 - 2 \beta + \frac 15} \right)^2+ \left(|f(s)| s^{\frac \beta 2 + \frac 1{10}}\right)^2\leq 1; $$ $$\leqno{\rm (BS2)}\quad |b(s)|\leq {10} s^{-1}, \ \frac 1{10} s^{-\beta}\leq \l(s) \leq 10 s^{-\beta}, \ \frac 1{10} s^{1-\beta} \leq (1-\beta) x(s) \leq 10 s^{1-\beta}; $$ $$\leqno{\rm (BS3)}\quad \int_{y>0}y^{10}\e^2(s,y)dy\leq 10 \l^{-10} ,\quad \mathcal N_{i}(s) \leq s^{-\frac 52},\quad \|\e(s)\|_{H^1} \lesssim \delta(\alpha^*). $$ Moreover, \be \left| \frac {(1-\beta)}{s^{1-\beta}} x (s) - 1\right| +\left| s^{\beta} \l(s) -1\right| +\left| \frac {s}{\beta } b(s) -1\right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 1{10}}, \ee \be \l^{-1} \|\e_y(s)\|_{L^2}+ \|\e(s)\|_{L^2} \lesssim 1. \ee
nodes.statement_short: For suitable $(\l_0,b_0)$ the solution with the constructed data satisfies (BS1)-(BS3) for all $s\geq s_0$, and the parameters obey $\l\sim s^{-\beta}$, $x\sim\frac{s^{1-\beta}}{1-\beta}$, $b\sim\beta/s$.
assumptions: Let $s_0=s_0(\beta)>1$ large enough and set \be x_0= x (s_0)= \frac 1{(1-\beta)}{s_0^{1-\beta}}. \ee
Let $\e_0\in H^1$ be such that \be s_0^{10}\left[ \int_{y>0} y^{10} \e^2_0(y) dy+\|\e_0\|^2_{H^1} \right]<1, \quad (\e_0, y {\Lambda} Q )=(\e_0,\Lambda Q) =(\e_0,Q)=0.\ee
conclusions: Then, there exists \be (\l_0,b_0)\in\mathcal D =\left \{(\l,b) \ : \ | \l - s_0^{-\beta}| \leq s_0^{-\beta - \frac 1{10}}, \ |b - \beta s_0^{-1}| \leq s_0^{-1-\frac 1{10}}\right\}, \ee such that the solution of \eqref{kdv} with initial data \be u_0(x) = \frac 1{\l^{\frac 12}_0} \left( Q_{b_0} + \l^{\frac 12}_0 q_0(s_0,x_0) \Yz+ \e_0 \right) \left( \frac {x-x_0}{\l_0}\right) +q_0(s_0,x) \ee has a decomposition $(b(s),\l(s),x(s), \e(s))$ as in Proposition \ref{le:2} which satisfies\footnote{recall that $s=s(t)$ is the rescaled time \fref{rescaledtime}.} on $[s_0,+\infty)$: $$\leqno{\rm (BS1)}\quad \left(|g(s)| s^{1 - 2 \beta + \frac 15} \right)^2+ \left(|f(s)| s^{\frac \beta 2 + \frac 1{10}}\right)^2\leq 1; $$ $$\leqno{\rm (BS2)}\quad |b(s)|\leq {10} s^{-1}, \ \frac 1{10} s^{-\beta}\leq \l(s) \leq 10 s^{-\beta}, \ \frac 1{10} s^{1-\beta} \leq (1-\beta) x(s) \leq 10 s^{1-\beta}; $$ $$\leqno{\rm (BS3)}\quad \int_{y>0}y^{10}\e^2(s,y)dy\leq 10 \l^{-10} ,\quad \mathcal N_{i}(s) \leq s^{-\frac 52},\quad \|\e(s)\|_{H^1} \lesssim \delta(\alpha^*). $$
Moreover, \be \left| \frac {(1-\beta)}{s^{1-\beta}} x (s) - 1\right| +\left| s^{\beta} \l(s) -1\right| +\left| \frac {s}{\beta } b(s) -1\right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 1{10}}, \ee

nodes.name: Initial value of the translation parameter $x_0$
nodes.statement: \be x_0= x (s_0)= \frac 1{(1-\beta)}{s_0^{1-\beta}}. \ee

nodes.name: Initial smallness and orthogonality of $\e_0$
nodes.statement: Let $\e_0\in H^1$ be such that \be s_0^{10}\left[ \int_{y>0} y^{10} \e^2_0(y) dy+\|\e_0\|^2_{H^1} \right]<1, \quad (\e_0, y {\Lambda} Q )=(\e_0,\Lambda Q) =(\e_0,Q)=0.\ee
nodes.statement_short: The initial remainder is $s_0^{-10}$-small in the weighted $H^1$ norm and satisfies the three orthogonality conditions.

nodes.name: Leading order behavior of the scaling parameter
nodes.statement: Let us observe that \fref{sharp} now gives the leading order behavior of the scaling parameter $\lambda(s)=\frac{1}{s^{\beta}}(1+o(1))$, and the conclusion of Theorem \ref{th:1} now immediately follow from the change of variables \fref{rescaledtime} depending on the value of $\beta$ as in step (iv) of section \ref{vneovnoen}.
nodes.statement_short: \eqref{sharp} gives $\l(s)=s^{-\beta}(1+o(1))$, from which Theorem 1.1 follows by the change of variables of step (iv).

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.1 (Bootstrap)
nodes.statement:
The rest of this section is therefore devoted to the proof of Proposition ef{PR:BS}. First observe by uniqueness of the decomposition that $$ b_0=b(s_0),\quad \l(s_0)=\l_0 \quad x(s_0)=x_0, \quad \e(s_0)=\e_0. $$ We now argue by contradiction, assuming that for all $(\l_0,b_0)\in \mathcal D$, we have $$ s^*(\l_0,b_0) := \sup \left\{ s\geq s_0 \hbox{ such that (BS1)-(BS2)-(BS3) holds on $[s_0,s]$} ight\} <+\infty. $$ We will derive a contradiction by first closing the bootstrap bounds (BS1)-(BS2)-(BS3), and then finding a couple $(\l_0,b_0)$ using a topological argument. \subsection{First consequences of the bootstrap bounds} Let us start with some quantitative bounds which follow from the bootstrap bounds and Proposition ef{le:2}.  egin{claim}[Consequences of the bootstrap estimates] {m (i)} For $s_0=s_0( eta)$ large enough, there holds:  egin{itemize} \item if $ eta> rac 13$, for all $s\in (s_0,s^*)$, $t(s)= \int_{s_0}^{s} \l^3(s') ds'<1$; \item if $0< eta\leq  rac 13$, for all $t>0$, $x(t) \geq  rac 23 t +  rac 23 {x_0}$. \end{itemize} {m (ii)} For all $s\in (s_0,s^*)$,  e 0< -p(s) \lesssim  rac 1 s,\quad  rac {\l}{x} \lesssim  rac 1 s, \ee  e \left|\lsl +bight| + \left| \xsl - 1ight| \lesssim \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} ight)^{ rac 12} +  rac 1{s^2},\ee  e \left| \lsl ight| \lesssim  rac 1 s + \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} ight)^{ rac 12},\quad \left| x_s ight| \lesssim s^{- eta}\left( 1+\left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} ight)^{ rac 12} ight) , \ee  e |b_s|+ |p_s| \lesssim \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} +  rac 1{s^2}, \ee  egin{align} & \left|  rac d{ds} \left( rac b{\l^2} + rac 4{\left(\int Qight)}c_0 \l^{- rac 32}(s) x^{-	heta}(s)ight) ight| 
onumber \ &\lesssim  rac 1{\l^2} \left(  rac 1{s^{ rac {29}{10}}} +  rac 1 s \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} ight)^{ rac 12} + \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}}ight). \end{align} {m (iii)} For all $s\in (s_0,s^*)$,  egin{align} &\|\e(s)\|_{L^2}^2 \lesssim \left| \int u^2(0) - \int Q^2ight|+ s^{-1} + x_0^{-	heta+ rac 12},\ &  rac 1{\l^2} \|\e_y(s)\|_{L^2}^2 \lesssim |E(u(0))|+ s^{-  rac 1{10}} + x_0^{-	heta- rac 12} . \end{align} \end{claim}  egin{proof} Let $ rac 13 < eta< rac {11}{20}$. Then $$ t(s) = \int_{s_0}^{s} \l^3(s') ds' \leq 10^3 \int_{s_0}^{s} (s')^{-3  eta} ds' \leq  rac {10^3} {3 eta-1} \left(s_0^{-3 eta+1}-s^{-3 eta +1}ight) <1 $$ for $s_0$ large enough. For $ eta =  rac 13$, $$ t(s) = \int_{s_0}^{s} \l^3(s') ds' \leq 10^3\, \log rac s{s_0} \quad \hbox{so that} \quad s \geq s_0 e^{10^{-3} t}. $$ Thus, $$ x(s) \geq  rac 3{20} s^{ rac 23} \geq  rac 3{20} s_0^{ rac 23} e^{ rac 23 10^{-3} t}\geq 10 t^3 . $$ for $s_0$ large enough. Since $x(s) \geq  rac 45 x_0$, we obtain $x(t) > t^3 +  rac 12 x_0$. Finally, for $0< eta < rac 13$, $$ t(s) = \int_{s_0}^{s} \l^3(s') ds' \leq  rac {10^3} {1-3 eta} \left(s^{1-3 eta}-s_0^{1-3 eta}ight) $$ so that for $s_0$ large $$s \geq \left(  rac {(1-3 eta) t}{10^3}+s_0^{1-3 eta}ight)^{ rac 1 {1-3 eta}} \geq 100 t^{ rac {1+ eta}{1- eta}}, $$ and $$x(s) \geq  rac 3{20} s^{1- eta} \geq 15 t^{1+ eta}.$$ Since $x(s) \geq  rac 45 x_0$, we obtain $x(t) > t^{1+ eta} +  rac 23 x_0$.\ The estimate \eqref{BSp} is a consequence of \eqref{cl.1bis} and $ rac  eta 2 + (1- eta) 	heta = 1$, so that $$ 0< p \lesssim \l^{ rac 12 } x^{-	heta} (s) \lesssim s^{- rac  eta 2} s^{-	heta (1- eta)} \lesssim  rac 1s. $$ The estimates \eqref{BSlsl}-\eqref{BSfond} are immediate consequences of \eqref{eq:2002bis}-\eqref{fond}, \eqref{cl.2tri}, the bootstrap assumptions and the upper bound $ eta< rac {11}{20}$. \end{proof} \subsection{Closing the estimates on $\e$} We now close the bounds on $\e$ and claim the improved bound: for all $s\in [s_0,s^*]$, $$\leqno{m (BS3')}\quad \int_{y>0}y^{10}\e^2(s,x)dx\leq 5 \l^{-10} ,\quad \mathcal N_{i}(s) \leq  rac 12 s^{- rac 52},\quad \|\e(s)\|_{H^1} \lesssim \delta(\alpha^*). $$ Let $\varphi_{10}$ be a smooth function such that $$\varphi_{10}(y)=\left\{ egin{array}{ll} 0\ \ \mbox{for}\ \ y\leq 0, \ y^{10}\ \ \mbox{for}\ \ y\geq 1\end{array}ight., \quad 0\leq \varphi_{10}\lesssim \varphi_{10}' \hbox{ for $0<y<1$}.$$ The control of the tail of $\e$ on the right is a direct consequence of the following brute force monotoncity formula:  egin{lemma}[Dynamical control of the tail on the right] For all $s\in [s_0,s^*]$, e {\l^{-10}} rac{d}{ds}\left\{\l^{10}\int\varphi_{10}\e^2ight\}\lesssim \mathcal N_{1,m loc}+ rac 1{s^2}. \ee \end{lemma} See proof of Lemma ef{lemmatail} in Appendix ef{appA}. \ The control of $\mathcal N_i(\e)$ norm, which is fundamental for the proof, now follows by adapting the mixed Energy/Morawetz monotonicity formula first derived in \cite{MMR1}. Recall the definitions  ref{defphi1bis},  ref{defphi2}, we claim:  egin{lemma}[Monotonicity formula] There exist $\mu>0$ such that the following holds for $B>100$ large enough. Let the energy--virial Lyapounov functionals for $i=1,2$,  egin{align} {\cal F}_{i} & = \int \Big[\varepsilon_y^2\psi_B + \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{i,B} \ &-  rac 13 \left((\varepsilon {+} Q_b{+}p\Yz{+}q)^6 - (Q_b{+}p\Yz{+}q)^6 - 6 \varepsilon \left(Q_b^5{+}q^5{+}5Q^4(p\Yz{+}q)ight)ight)\psi_B\Big] .
onumber \end{align} Then the following estimates hold on $[s_0, s^*]$:\ {\em (i) Lyapounov control}: for $i=1,2$, $j\geq 0$  e  rac{d}{ds}\left[ s^j {\mathcal F_{i}} ight]+ {\mu} s^j \int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\e^2ight) \varphi'_{i,B} \lesssim s^{j-4} +s^{j-9+10  eta} . \ee {\em (iii) Coercivity of $\mathcal F_{i}$ and pointwise bounds}: for $i=1,2$, $j\geq 0$,  egin{equation} - rac 1{s^4} + \mathcal N_i \lesssim \mathcal F_{i}\lesssim  rac 1{s^4} + \mathcal N_i .\end{equation} \end{lemma} See the proof of Lemma ef{propasymtp} in Appendix ef{appA}. \ 
oindent 	extbf{Proof of {m (BS3')}.} From Lemma ef{lemmatail}, (BS2) and (BS3), $$  rac d{ds} \left\{ \l^{10} \int \varphi_{10} \e^2 ight\} \lesssim \l^{10}\left(\mathcal N_{1,m loc} + s^{-2}ight) \lesssim s^{-10  eta -2}, $$ so that by integration on $[s_0,s]$, and \eqref{A2}, $$ \l^{10}(s)\int \varphi_{10} \e^2(s) \leq \l^{10}(s_0) \int \varphi_{10} \e^2(s_0) + Cs_0^{-1-10 eta} \leq 2. $$ By the properties of $\varphi_{10}$ and \eqref{A2}, we obtain  e \l^{10}(s) \int_{y>0}y^{10} \e^2(s,y) dy \leq 3. \ee Now, we apply Lemma ef{propasymtp} with $j= rac 52 $. We find by \eqref{lyapounovconrolbis} and $ eta<  rac {11}{20}$,  e  rac d{ds} \left[ s^{ rac 52} \mathcal F_iight] \lesssim s^{- rac 32} + s^{-1-10 ( rac {11}{20}- eta)}. \ee The initial smallness  ref{A2} ensures $$s_0^{10}|\mathcal F_i(0)|\lesssim 1$$ and thus the time integration of  ref{neovneogbgeo} on $[s_0,s^*]$ yields: $$ \mathcal F_i (s)\lesssim s^{-  rac 52} s_0^{-\delta} $$ for some $\delta=\delta( eta)>0$. Using \eqref{lowerbound}, we conclude: $$ \mathcal N_i(s) \leq s^{-  rac 52} s_0^{-\delta} +s^{-4} \leq  rac 12 s^{-  rac 52} $$ for $s_0$ large enough, which together with \eqref{aa3} and the control of the full $H^1$ norm through the conservation laws  ref{twobound},  ref{energbound} concludes the proof of (BS3'). \subsection{Closing the estimates on $(b,\l,x)$} We now use the obtained bounds on $\e$ and the modulation equations on the geometrical parameters of Proposition ef{le:2} to close the bounds on $(b,\l,x)$. We claim: for all $s\in [s_0,s^*]$,$$\leqno{m (BS2')}\quad |b(s)|\leq {5} s^{-1}, \  rac 1{5} s^{- eta}\leq \l(s) \leq 5 s^{- eta}, \  rac 1{5} s^{1- eta} \leq (1- eta) x(s) \leq 5 s^{1- eta}. $$ \ 	extbf{Proof of (BS2').} First, note that from \eqref{fond}, \eqref{eq:2002bis}, and using (BS2)-(BS3), $ rac 13 \leq  eta\leq  rac 9{10}$, we have on $[s_0,s^*]$:  e \left| g_s ight| \lesssim s^{- rac 9 4 + 2  eta }, \ee  e \left| \lsl + b ight| \lesssim s^{- rac 54}, \ee  e \left| \xsl -1 ight|\lesssim s^{- rac 54}. \ee By (BS1) and (BS2), we have using $(1- eta)(	heta-1) = rac  eta 2$ the estimate:  egin{align} & \left| \l (s) - \left( rac 2 {\int Q} c_0  rac {1}{	heta-1}ight)^2 {x^{-2 	heta+2}(s)} ight| \ &= \left| \l^{ rac 12} (s) +  rac 2 {\int Q} c_0  rac {1}{	heta-1} {x^{-	heta+1}(s)}ight| \left| \l^{ rac 12} (s) -  rac 2 {\int Q} c_0  rac {1}{	heta-1} {x^{-	heta+1}(s)}ight|
onumber \ &\lesssim |f(s)| \left( \l^{ rac 12} (s)+x^{-	heta+1}(s)ight) \lesssim s^{- rac  eta 2 -  rac 1{10} } \left( s^{- rac  eta 2} + s^{-(1- eta)(	heta-1)}ight) \lesssim s^{-  eta -  rac 1{10}}.
onumber \end{align} Using \eqref{dx}, we find $$ \left| x_s (s) - \left( rac 2 {\int Q} c_0  rac {1}{	heta-1}ight)^2 {x^{-2 	heta+2}(s)} ight| \lesssim s^{-  eta -  rac 1{10}} + s^{- rac 54 -  eta } \lesssim s^{-  eta -  rac 1{10}}. $$ and hence e \left| \left(x^{ rac 1{1- eta}}ight)_s - (1- eta)^{-(1- eta)} ight| \lesssim s^{- rac 1{10}}, \ee from $2	heta-1= rac 1{1- eta}$ and the choice of $c_0$ in  ref{defcobeta} which gives: $$ (1- eta)^{-(1- eta)}= (2	heta-1)\left( rac 2 {\int Q} c_0  rac {1}{	heta-1}ight)^2. $$ Since from  ref{initixzero}: $$  rac {(1- eta) }{s_0^{1- eta}} x (s_0)= 1,$$ the time integration of  ref{vnkrvrnorn} on $[s_0,s]$ yields $$ \left|x^{ rac 1{ eta-1}}(s) - (1- eta)^{- rac 1{ eta-1}} s ight| \lesssim s^{1- rac 1{10}}. $$ Thus,  e \left|  rac {(1- eta)}{s^{1- eta}} x (s) - 1ight| \lesssim s^{- rac 1{10}}. \ee Inserting \eqref{aa2} into \eqref{bbb2}, we find for $\l$,  e \left| s^{ eta} \l(s) -1ight| \lesssim s^{- rac 1{10}}. \ee Finally, using $|g(s)| \leq s^{-1 + 2  eta -  rac 1{5}}$, we find  e \left|  rac {s}{ eta } b(s) -1ight| \lesssim s^{- rac 1{10}}. \ee From \eqref{aa2}, \eqref{aaa2} and \eqref{aaaa2}, (BS2') follows for $s_0$ large enough. \subsection{Choice of $\l_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument} We now claim from a standard topological argument based on the ougoing behavior of the ODE's for $(f,g)$ that we can find $(b_0,\l_0)\in \mathcal D$ such that the remaining condition $(BS1)$ is closed.\ Indeed, let $$ G(s) = g(s) s^{1-2  eta +  rac 1{5}},\quad F(s) = f(s) s^{ rac  eta 2+  rac 1{10}}, $$ and $$ H(s) = F^2(s) + G^2(s). $$ From (BS2') and (BS3'), since $s^*=s^*(x_0,b_0)<+\infty$, it follows from a standard continuity argument that at $s=s^* \geq s_0,$  e H(s^*)=1. \ee We first claim the strict outgoing behavior:  e H'(s^*)\geq  rac {1}{20 s^*}. \ee \emph{Proof of \eqref{dFdG}.} Since $$ G'(s) = \left(1- 2  eta + rac 1{5}ight) g(s)s^{-2  eta +  rac 1{5}} +g'(s) s^{1-2  eta +  rac 1{5}}, $$ we have using  ref{dFdG}:  e G'(s^*)= \left(1- 2  eta + rac 1{5}ight)  rac {G(s^*)}{s^*} +O\left((s^*)^{-(1+ rac 1{20})}ight). \ee Similarly, $$ F'(s^*)= \left( rac  eta 2+  rac 1{10}ight) f(s^*) (s^*)^{ rac  eta 2+  rac 1{10}-1} + f'(s^*) (s^*)^{ rac  eta 2+  rac 1{10}}. $$ We now estimate $f'(s)$. By direct computations and then \eqref{dl}, \eqref{dx} and (BS1)-(BS2),  egin{align*} f'(s) &=  rac 12  rac {\l_s}{\l} \l^{ rac 12} -  rac 2{\int Q}c_0 x_s x^{-	heta} \ & =  rac 12 \l^{ rac 52} \left[  rac b{\l^2} -  rac 4{\int Q} c_0 \l^{- rac 32} x^{-	heta}ight] +O\left(s^{- rac 54- rac  eta 2}ight) \ &=  rac 12 \l^{ rac 52} g(s) + O\left(s^{- rac 54- rac  eta 2}ight) = O\left(s^{-1 - rac  eta 2 - rac 1{5}}ight). \end{align*} Thus,  e F'(s^*)=\left( rac  eta 2+  rac 1{10}ight)  rac {F(s^*)} {s^*} + O\left( (s^*)^{-1- rac 1{10}} ight). \ee Therefore $$ H'(s^*) = 2 F'(s^*)F(s^*) + 2 G'(s^*) G(s^*) \geq  rac 1{10}  rac {H(s^*)}{s^*} + O\left((s^*)^{-1- rac 1{20}}ight) \geq  rac 1{20s^*}, $$ for $s_0$ large enough. \medskip By standard arguments (see e.g. the proof of Lemma 6 in \cite{MMC}), the strict outgoing behavior  ref{dFdG} ensures that the map $(\l_0,b_0)\in \mathcal D 	o s^*(x_0,b_0)$ is continuous. We define the continuous maps  egin{align*} \l_0(F_0) &= s_0^{- eta}\left( 1 - F_0 s_0^{- rac 1{10}} ight)^2 \ b_0(F_0,G_0) &=  eta s_0^{-1+ rac  eta 2} \l_0^{ rac 12}(F_0 ) \left( 1+  rac 1 eta G_0 s_0^{ rac 32 eta -  rac 1{5}} \l_0^{ rac 32} (F_0) ight)\ & =  eta s_0^{-1} \left| 1 - F_0 s_0^{- rac 1{10}}ight| \left( 1+  rac 1 eta G_0 s_0^{-  rac 1{5}} \left| 1 - F_0 s_0^{- rac 1{10}}ight|^3 ight) \end{align*} so that  egin{align*} G_0 &= s_0^{1-2  eta + rac 1{5}} \left(  rac {b_0}{\l_0^2} -  rac 4{\int Q} c_0 \l_0^{- rac 32} x_0^{-	heta}ight)\ F_0 &= s_0^{ rac  eta 2 + rac 1{10}} \left( \l_0^{ rac 12} + rac 2{\int Q} c_0  rac 1{	heta-1} x_0^{-	heta+1} ight). \end{align*} Now, consider the continous map  egin{align*} \mathcal M \ : \ \ \ \mathcal B_{\RR^2} &	o \mathcal S_{\RR^2} ,\ (F_0,G_0) &\mapsto \left(F(s^*(\l_0(F_0),b_0(F_0,G_0))), G(s^*(\l_0(F_0),b_0(F_0,G_0)))ight). \end{align*} where $\mathcal B_{\RR^2}$ and $\mathcal S_{\RR^2} $ are, respectively, the ball and the sphere of $\RR^2$ of radius $1$. For $(F_0,G_0)\in \mathcal S_{\RR^2}$, we have $\mathcal M(F_0,G_0) = (F_0,G_0)$, in other words, $\mathcal M$ is the identity on the sphere $\mathcal S_{\RR^2}$. The existence of such a continuous map $\mathcal M$ is in contradiction with Brouwer's fixed point theorem. Therefore, there exists $\l_0$ and $b_0$ such that  e | \l_0 - s_0^{- eta}| \leq s_0^{- eta -  rac 1{10}}, \quad |b_0 -  eta s_0^{-1}| \leq s_0^{-1-  rac 1{10}}, \ee and $s^*(\l_0,b_0)=+\infty$. In particular (BS1)-(BS2)-(BS3) hold on $[s_0,+\infty)$.\ Finally, \eqref{aa2}, \eqref{aaa2} and \eqref{aaaa2} imply \eqref{sharp}.\ This concludes the proof of Proposition ef{PR:BS} and therefore also of Theorem ef{th:1}.
nodes.statement_short: Argue by contradiction on $s^*<\infty$: close (BS3) then (BS2) strictly, then use the strict outgoing behavior of $H=F^2+G^2$ and Brouwer's theorem to select $(\l_0,b_0)$ with $s^*=+\infty$.

nodes.name: Contradiction setup and definition of the exit time $s^*$
nodes.statement: The rest of this section is therefore devoted to the proof of Proposition \ref{PR:BS}. First observe by uniqueness of the decomposition that $$ b_0=b(s_0),\quad \l(s_0)=\l_0 \quad x(s_0)=x_0, \quad \e(s_0)=\e_0. $$ We now argue by contradiction, assuming that for all $(\l_0,b_0)\in \mathcal D$, we have $$ s^*(\l_0,b_0) := \sup \left\{ s\geq s_0 \hbox{ such that (BS1)-(BS2)-(BS3) holds on $[s_0,s]$} \right\} <+\infty. $$ We will derive a contradiction by first closing the bootstrap bounds (BS1)-(BS2)-(BS3), and then finding a couple $(\l_0,b_0)$ using a topological argument.
nodes.statement_short: Assume $s^*(\l_0,b_0)<+\infty$ for every $(\l_0,b_0)\in\mathcal D$ and announce the two-part strategy.

nodes.name: First consequences of the bootstrap bounds
nodes.statement: Let us start with some quantitative bounds which follow from the bootstrap bounds and Proposition \ref{le:2}. \begin{claim}[Consequences of the bootstrap estimates] {\rm (i)} For $s_0=s_0(\beta)$ large enough, there holds: \begin{itemize} \item if $\beta>\frac 13$, for all $s\in (s_0,s^*)$, $t(s)= \int_{s_0}^{s} \l^3(s') ds'<1$; \item if $0<\beta\leq \frac 13$, for all $t>0$, $x(t) \geq \frac 23 t + \frac 23 {x_0}$. \end{itemize} {\rm (ii)} For all $s\in (s_0,s^*)$, \be 0< -p(s) \lesssim \frac 1 s,\quad \frac {\l}{x} \lesssim \frac 1 s, \ee \be \left|\lsl +b\right| + \left| \xsl - 1\right| \lesssim \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} + \frac 1{s^2},\ee \be \left| \lsl \right| \lesssim \frac 1 s + \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12},\quad \left| x_s \right| \lesssim s^{-\beta}\left( 1+\left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} \right) , \ee \be |b_s|+ |p_s| \lesssim \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} + \frac 1{s^2}, \ee \begin{align} & \left| \frac d{ds} \left(\frac b{\l^2} +\frac 4{\left(\int Q\right)}c_0 \l^{-\frac 32}(s) x^{-\theta}(s)\right) \right| \nonumber \\ &\lesssim \frac 1{\l^2} \left( \frac 1{s^{\frac {29}{10}}} + \frac 1 s \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} + \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}}\right). \end{align} {\rm (iii)} For all $s\in (s_0,s^*)$, \begin{align} &\|\e(s)\|_{L^2}^2 \lesssim \left| \int u^2(0) - \int Q^2\right|+ s^{-1} + x_0^{-\theta+\frac 12},\\ & \frac 1{\l^2} \|\e_y(s)\|_{L^2}^2 \lesssim |E(u(0))|+ s^{- \frac 1{10}} + x_0^{-\theta-\frac 12} . \end{align} \end{claim} \begin{proof} Let $\frac 13 <\beta<\frac {11}{20}$. Then $$ t(s) = \int_{s_0}^{s} \l^3(s') ds' \leq 10^3 \int_{s_0}^{s} (s')^{-3 \beta} ds' \leq \frac {10^3} {3\beta-1} \left(s_0^{-3\beta+1}-s^{-3\beta +1}\right) <1 $$ for $s_0$ large enough. For $\beta = \frac 13$, $$ t(s) = \int_{s_0}^{s} \l^3(s') ds' \leq 10^3\, \log\frac s{s_0} \quad \hbox{so that} \quad s \geq s_0 e^{10^{-3} t}. $$ Thus, $$ x(s) \geq \frac 3{20} s^{\frac 23} \geq \frac 3{20} s_0^{\frac 23} e^{\frac 23 10^{-3} t}\geq 10 t^3 . $$ for $s_0$ large enough. Since $x(s) \geq \frac 45 x_0$, we obtain $x(t) > t^3 + \frac 12 x_0$. Finally, for $0<\beta <\frac 13$, $$ t(s) = \int_{s_0}^{s} \l^3(s') ds' \leq \frac {10^3} {1-3\beta} \left(s^{1-3\beta}-s_0^{1-3\beta}\right) $$ so that for $s_0$ large $$s \geq \left( \frac {(1-3\beta) t}{10^3}+s_0^{1-3\beta}\right)^{\frac 1 {1-3\beta}} \geq 100 t^{\frac {1+\beta}{1-\beta}}, $$ and $$x(s) \geq \frac 3{20} s^{1-\beta} \geq 15 t^{1+\beta}.$$ Since $x(s) \geq \frac 45 x_0$, we obtain $x(t) > t^{1+\beta} + \frac 23 x_0$.\\ The estimate \eqref{BSp} is a consequence of \eqref{cl.1bis} and $\frac \beta 2 + (1-\beta) \theta = 1$, so that $$ 0< p \lesssim \l^{\frac 12 } x^{-\theta} (s) \lesssim s^{-\frac \beta 2} s^{-\theta (1-\beta)} \lesssim \frac 1s. $$ The estimates \eqref{BSlsl}-\eqref{BSfond} are immediate consequences of \eqref{eq:2002bis}-\eqref{fond}, \eqref{cl.2tri}, the bootstrap assumptions and the upper bound $\beta<\frac {11}{20}$. \end{proof}
nodes.statement_short: Derive Claim 2: the time transformation stays in range, $|p|\lesssim 1/s$, and all modulation quantities are controlled by $\int\e^2e^{-|y|/10}+s^{-2}$.
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds

nodes.name: Closing the estimates on $\e$
nodes.statement: We now close the bounds on $\e$ and claim the improved bound: for all $s\in [s_0,s^*]$, $$\leqno{\rm (BS3')}\quad \int_{y>0}y^{10}\e^2(s,x)dx\leq 5 \l^{-10} ,\quad \mathcal N_{i}(s) \leq \frac 12 s^{-\frac 52},\quad \|\e(s)\|_{H^1} \lesssim \delta(\alpha^*). $$ Let $\varphi_{10}$ be a smooth function such that $$\varphi_{10}(y)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll} 0\ \ \mbox{for}\ \ y\leq 0, \\ y^{10}\ \ \mbox{for}\ \ y\geq 1\end{array}\right., \quad 0\leq \varphi_{10}\lesssim \varphi_{10}' \hbox{ for $0<y<1$}.$$ The control of the tail of $\e$ on the right is a direct consequence of the following brute force monotoncity formula: \begin{lemma}[Dynamical control of the tail on the right] For all $s\in [s_0,s^*]$,\be {\l^{-10}}\frac{d}{ds}\left\{\l^{10}\int\varphi_{10}\e^2\right\}\lesssim \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}+\frac 1{s^2}. \ee \end{lemma} See proof of Lemma \ref{lemmatail} in Appendix \ref{appA}. \\ The control of $\mathcal N_i(\e)$ norm, which is fundamental for the proof, now follows by adapting the mixed Energy/Morawetz monotonicity formula first derived in \cite{MMR1}. Recall the definitions \fref{defphi1bis}, \fref{defphi2}, we claim: \begin{lemma}[Monotonicity formula] There exist $\mu>0$ such that the following holds for $B>100$ large enough. Let the energy--virial Lyapounov functionals for $i=1,2$, \begin{align} {\cal F}_{i} & = \int \Big[\varepsilon_y^2\psi_B + \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{i,B} \\ &- \frac 13 \left((\varepsilon {+} Q_b{+}p\Yz{+}q)^6 - (Q_b{+}p\Yz{+}q)^6 - 6 \varepsilon \left(Q_b^5{+}q^5{+}5Q^4(p\Yz{+}q)\right)\right)\psi_B\Big] .\nonumber \end{align} Then the following estimates hold on $[s_0, s^*]$:\\ {\em (i) Lyapounov control}: for $i=1,2$, $j\geq 0$ \be \frac{d}{ds}\left[ s^j {\mathcal F_{i}} \right]+ {\mu} s^j \int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\e^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B} \lesssim s^{j-4} +s^{j-9+10 \beta} . \ee {\em (iii) Coercivity of $\mathcal F_{i}$ and pointwise bounds}: for $i=1,2$, $j\geq 0$, \begin{equation} -\frac 1{s^4} + \mathcal N_i \lesssim \mathcal F_{i}\lesssim \frac 1{s^4} + \mathcal N_i .\end{equation} \end{lemma} See the proof of Lemma \ref{propasymtp} in Appendix \ref{appA}. \\ \noindent \textbf{Proof of {\rm (BS3')}.} From Lemma \ref{lemmatail}, (BS2) and (BS3), $$ \frac d{ds} \left\{ \l^{10} \int \varphi_{10} \e^2 \right\} \lesssim \l^{10}\left(\mathcal N_{1,\rm loc} + s^{-2}\right) \lesssim s^{-10 \beta -2}, $$ so that by integration on $[s_0,s]$, and \eqref{A2}, $$ \l^{10}(s)\int \varphi_{10} \e^2(s) \leq \l^{10}(s_0) \int \varphi_{10} \e^2(s_0) + Cs_0^{-1-10\beta} \leq 2. $$ By the properties of $\varphi_{10}$ and \eqref{A2}, we obtain \be \l^{10}(s) \int_{y>0}y^{10} \e^2(s,y) dy \leq 3. \ee Now, we apply Lemma \ref{propasymtp} with $j=\frac 52 $. We find by \eqref{lyapounovconrolbis} and $\beta< \frac {11}{20}$, \be \frac d{ds} \left[ s^{\frac 52} \mathcal F_i\right] \lesssim s^{-\frac 32} + s^{-1-10 (\frac {11}{20}-\beta)}. \ee The initial smallness \fref{A2} ensures $$s_0^{10}|\mathcal F_i(0)|\lesssim 1$$ and thus the time integration of \fref{neovneogbgeo} on $[s_0,s^*]$ yields: $$ \mathcal F_i (s)\lesssim s^{- \frac 52} s_0^{-\delta} $$ for some $\delta=\delta(\beta)>0$. Using \eqref{lowerbound}, we conclude: $$ \mathcal N_i(s) \leq s^{- \frac 52} s_0^{-\delta} +s^{-4} \leq \frac 12 s^{- \frac 52} $$ for $s_0$ large enough, which together with \eqref{aa3} and the control of the full $H^1$ norm through the conservation laws \fref{twobound}, \fref{energbound} concludes the proof of (BS3').
nodes.statement_short: Use the tail monotonicity of Lemma 3.2 and the energy-virial Lyapounov control of Lemma 3.3 to improve (BS3) into (BS3').

nodes.name: Closing the estimates on $(b,\l,x)$
nodes.statement: We now use the obtained bounds on $\e$ and the modulation equations on the geometrical parameters of Proposition \ref{le:2} to close the bounds on $(b,\l,x)$. We claim: for all $s\in [s_0,s^*]$,$$\leqno{\rm (BS2')}\quad |b(s)|\leq {5} s^{-1}, \ \frac 1{5} s^{-\beta}\leq \l(s) \leq 5 s^{-\beta}, \ \frac 1{5} s^{1-\beta} \leq (1-\beta) x(s) \leq 5 s^{1-\beta}. $$ \\ \textbf{Proof of (BS2').} First, note that from \eqref{fond}, \eqref{eq:2002bis}, and using (BS2)-(BS3), $\frac 13 \leq \beta\leq \frac 9{10}$, we have on $[s_0,s^*]$: \be \left| g_s \right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 9 4 + 2 \beta }, \ee \be \left| \lsl + b \right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 54}, \ee \be \left| \xsl -1 \right|\lesssim s^{-\frac 54}. \ee By (BS1) and (BS2), we have using $(1-\beta)(\theta-1) =\frac \beta 2$ the estimate: \begin{align} & \left| \l (s) - \left(\frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1}\right)^2 {x^{-2 \theta+2}(s)} \right| \\ &= \left| \l^{\frac 12} (s) + \frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1} {x^{-\theta+1}(s)}\right| \left| \l^{\frac 12} (s) - \frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1} {x^{-\theta+1}(s)}\right|\nonumber \\ &\lesssim |f(s)| \left( \l^{\frac 12} (s)+x^{-\theta+1}(s)\right) \lesssim s^{-\frac \beta 2 - \frac 1{10} } \left( s^{-\frac \beta 2} + s^{-(1-\beta)(\theta-1)}\right) \lesssim s^{- \beta - \frac 1{10}}.\nonumber \end{align} Using \eqref{dx}, we find $$ \left| x_s (s) - \left(\frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1}\right)^2 {x^{-2 \theta+2}(s)} \right| \lesssim s^{- \beta - \frac 1{10}} + s^{-\frac 54 - \beta } \lesssim s^{- \beta - \frac 1{10}}. $$ and hence\be \left| \left(x^{\frac 1{1-\beta}}\right)_s - (1-\beta)^{-(1-\beta)} \right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 1{10}}, \ee from $2\theta-1=\frac 1{1-\beta}$ and the choice of $c_0$ in \fref{defcobeta} which gives: $$ (1-\beta)^{-(1-\beta)}= (2\theta-1)\left(\frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1}\right)^2. $$ Since from \fref{initixzero}: $$ \frac {(1-\beta) }{s_0^{1-\beta}} x (s_0)= 1,$$ the time integration of \fref{vnkrvrnorn} on $[s_0,s]$ yields $$ \left|x^{\frac 1{\beta-1}}(s) -
